milestones.title: DENDRAL program infers molecular structures from mass spectra
milestones.summary: Stanford's DENDRAL, begun in 1965 by Joshua Lederberg, Edward Feigenbaum and Carl Djerassi, generated candidate molecular structures and pruned those that did not fit mass-spectrometry data. Once fully working it did this faster than an expert spectrometrist with comparable accuracy. Its offshoot Meta-DENDRAL inferred fragmentation rules from data (J. Am. Chem. Soc., 1976).
milestones.why_it_matters: It was the first sustained attempt to make a computer form scientific hypotheses, and became the template for expert systems and later AI tools in chemistry.

sources.label: Artificial Intelligence journal, 1993 (DENDRAL case study by its creators)
J. Am. Chem. Soc., 1976 (Meta-DENDRAL rule discovery)
US National Library of Medicine, Lederberg Papers profile

milestones.title: EQP automated prover proves the Robbins conjecture
milestones.summary: William McCune's EQP theorem prover at Argonne National Laboratory proved, on 10 October 1996, the last missing step (Winker's condition) showing every Robbins algebra is Boolean, settling a question posed in the 1930s. The search took about eight days on an RS/6000 processor; the proof appeared in the Journal of Automated Reasoning in 1997.

before_after.metric: Status of the Robbins problem

milestones.why_it_matters: The first famous open mathematical question settled by an automated reasoning program, showing a machine could find a proof that experienced mathematicians had missed.

sources.label: McCune, Robbins Algebras Are Boolean (posted October 1996)

milestones.title: Golem project evolves robot bodies and brains in simulation, then prints them
milestones.summary: Brandeis researchers evolved simple machines made of bars, actuators and artificial neurons inside a physics simulation, keeping the designs that moved best. The fittest designs were then fabricated with rapid-prototyping (3D printing) machines and crawled in the real world. The authors called them the first robots both designed and built by machines.
milestones.why_it_matters: Robots had always been designed piece by piece by engineers. Letting a search process invent both body and controller started the line of work that leads to AI-designed robots and organisms.
ai_systems: Evolutionary algorithm with neural-network controllers (Golem project)

milestones.title: Rosetta designs Top7, a protein with a fold not seen in nature
milestones.summary: Baker's group used Rosetta, a program that alternates between designing a sequence and predicting its structure, to design Top7, a 93-residue protein with a new topology. Top7 folded and was extremely stable. Its X-ray structure matched the computer design to 1.2 angstroms RMSD.
milestones.why_it_matters: A computer invented a working protein from first principles instead of editing a natural one. The 2024 Chemistry Nobel background describes Top7 as the first protein entirely different from all known ones.

sources.label: Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2024, popular information (Top7)

milestones.title: Computer-evolved antenna flies on NASA's ST5, first evolved hardware in space
milestones.summary: NASA Ames used evolutionary algorithms and an antenna simulator to design an irregular bent-wire antenna for the three ST5 microsatellites, redesigning it within a month when the mission's orbit changed. On a spacecraft mock-up, two evolved antennas reached 93% efficiency versus 38% for two conventional helix antennas. It launched on 22 March 2006.

before_after.metric: Efficiency of the antenna pair on an ST5 spacecraft mock-up

milestones.why_it_matters: Automated search found a shape no engineer would draw, beat the hand-made design, and flew. It showed computer-invented designs could become flight-qualified hardware, not just paper ideas.

sources.label: AIAA Space 2006 conference paper (Hornby et al.), 2006-09-19
Full text, NASA Technical Reports Server

milestones.title: Robot scientist Adam autonomously discovers gene functions in yeast
milestones.summary: Adam, a laboratory robot, generated hypotheses about which yeast genes encode 'orphan' enzymes, designed and ran the experiments itself and interpreted the results; humans then confirmed its conclusions by hand. The study logged 6.6 million biomass measurements. Its makers called it the first machine to discover new scientific knowledge independently.
milestones.why_it_matters: It was the first closed loop of hypothesis, experiment and conclusion run by a machine, the template for today's self-driving labs and AI scientists.

milestones.title: Robot scientist Eve automates drug screening and finds antimalarial leads
milestones.summary: Eve, a lab robot that learns structure-activity models and picks which compounds to test next, was shown by econometric modelling to beat standard screening on cost. It found the anti-cancer compound TNP-470 potently inhibits malaria-parasite DHFR; a 2018 Eve screen found triclosan also hits DHFR, including pyrimethamine-resistant forms.
milestones.why_it_matters: Closing the loop between hypothesis and experiment inside a machine lowers the cost of searching for drugs against tropical diseases that markets neglect.

milestones.title: Algorithm Melvin designs quantum optics experiments that humans had not found
milestones.summary: The search program Melvin combined optical elements into new set-ups for complex entangled photon states, often using asymmetric tricks its authors found hard to understand intuitively. One of its designs was built in Vienna, giving the first entangled state where both the number of photons and the dimensions exceed two (three photons, 3×3×2).

before_after.metric: multi-photon entanglement with more than two particles and more than two dimensions
before_after.after: three-photon 3×3×2 state built from a computer-found design

milestones.why_it_matters: Experiments are usually invented by human intuition, which misses unusual layouts. A program that searches designs can reach set-ups people overlooked, which humans then build and test.

milestones.title: AlphaGo's move 37 surprises Go experts and helps beat Lee Sedol
milestones.summary: In game two of its match with Lee Sedol, winner of 18 world titles, DeepMind's AlphaGo played move 37, a move its own model rated as having about a 1 in 10,000 chance of being played by a human. Commentators were startled; Lee later called AlphaGo creative. AlphaGo won the game and the match 4-1.
milestones.why_it_matters: Widely seen as the first time a machine produced an idea that experts recognised as both original and good, challenging long-held human strategy in a game studied for millennia.

milestones.title: SAT solver settles the Boolean Pythagorean triples problem
milestones.summary: Heule, Kullmann and Marek showed the integers 1 to 7,824 can be coloured red and blue with no single-colour Pythagorean triple (a²+b²=c²), but 1 to 7,825 cannot. The cube-and-conquer SAT search ran about two days on 800 cores and produced a roughly 200 TB proof, checkable from a 68 GB certificate.

before_after.metric: Largest n where 1..n has a 2-colouring with no monochromatic Pythagorean triple

milestones.why_it_matters: A decades-old combinatorics question was settled by automated reasoning, with a proof that independent checking software can verify even though no human can read it.

milestones.title: Machine learning cuts energy used to cool a Google data centre by up to 40%
milestones.summary: DeepMind trained deep neural networks on historical data from thousands of data-centre sensors to recommend cooling settings, tested in a live Google data centre. Google reported up to 40% less cooling energy, a 15% cut in PUE overhead. By 2018 an autonomous version ran cooling in several data centres, saving about 30% on average.

before_after.metric: energy used for cooling
before_after.after: up to 40% lower (15% lower PUE overhead)

milestones.why_it_matters: Data centres use a growing share of the world's electricity, and cooling is a large part of it. Learned control can save energy in complex plants without new hardware.

milestones.title: ML-aided virtual screen of 1.6 million molecules finds efficient OLED emitters
milestones.summary: Harvard, MIT and Samsung researchers combined quantum chemistry, cheminformatics and a neural network to explore 1.6 million candidate OLED molecules, screening over 400,000 with time-dependent DFT. The team jointly picked the best candidates; those synthesized reached external quantum efficiencies as high as 22%.
milestones.why_it_matters: Display and lighting materials are usually found by slow trial and error. Computing hundreds of thousands of molecules first, then making a few, became a model for molecular discovery.
ai_systems: Neural-network property predictor within a TD-DFT screening funnel

milestones.title: Neural networks used to represent quantum many-body wavefunctions
milestones.summary: Carleo and Troyer showed that a neural network (a restricted Boltzmann machine) can serve as a variational wavefunction for interacting quantum spins. Trained with a reinforcement-learning scheme, it found ground states and simulated time evolution of prototypical 1D and 2D spin models with high accuracy, launching the 'neural quantum states' method.
milestones.why_it_matters: The information needed to describe many interacting quantum particles grows exponentially. Neural networks give compact descriptions, a new general tool for magnets, materials and molecules.

milestones.title: Learned models stand in for B-tree indexes, with faster lookups in tests
milestones.summary: Google and MIT researchers showed that the indexes databases use to find records can be replaced by models that predict where a record sits. On several real datasets, their learned indexes ran up to 70% faster than cache-optimized B-trees while using about ten times less memory, on read-only data.

before_after.metric: Lookup speed and memory vs cache-optimized B-tree

milestones.why_it_matters: Indexes sit under nearly every database and search engine. Treating them as prediction problems started a research field on letting the data itself shape core system components.
ai_systems: Learned index (neural network and recursive model index)
milestones.contested_note: Thomas Neumann (TU Munich, Database Architects blog, 2017-12-23) argued the B-tree baselines were weak and that an interpolating B-tree matches the reported speed. A later independent benchmark (Marcus et al., VLDB 2020) found learned indexes do beat tuned traditional indexes, but on read-only, in-memory data.

milestones.title: Neural network finds new planets around Kepler-90 and Kepler-80
milestones.summary: A convolutional neural network trained on labelled Kepler signals searched weak, previously overlooked transit signals and found Kepler-90i and Kepler-80g, both statistically validated as planets. Kepler-90 became the first known system with eight planets, tying the Solar System. On test data the model ranked real planets above false positives 98.8% of the time.

before_after.metric: Known planets orbiting Kepler-90

milestones.why_it_matters: Telescopes record far more faint signals than people can inspect. A trained classifier can reopen old data and pull out real planets that human-tuned searches missed.

milestones.title: Computer-planned syntheses of eight medicinal targets all succeed in the lab
milestones.summary: The Chematica program (later sold as Synthia) autonomously designed routes to eight diverse targets: seven commercially valuable bioactive substances and one natural product. Chemists executed all eight routes in the lab; they improved yields or costs, offered alternatives to patented routes, or made targets never synthesized before.
milestones.why_it_matters: It showed computer synthesis planning could do more than suggest single steps: complete routes worked at the bench and could beat human-designed ones on cost and yield.
organizations: UNIST / IBS Center for Soft and Living Matter

milestones.title: Deep networks plus tree search plan syntheses chemists rate equal to published
milestones.summary: Segler, Preuss and Waller trained deep neural networks on essentially all published organic reactions and combined them with Monte Carlo tree search. The system solved almost twice as many molecules, thirty times faster, than rule-based computer planning, and in a double-blind test chemists judged its routes equivalent to published ones.

before_after.metric: Target molecules solved vs. rule-based computer search

milestones.why_it_matters: Working out how to make a molecule is a core bottleneck in chemistry. Learning the rules from data instead of hand-coding them made automated synthesis planning practical.
ai_systems: 3N-MCTS (expansion policy and filter networks with Monte Carlo tree search)

milestones.title: FDA authorizes first autonomous AI diagnostic system (diabetic eye disease)
milestones.summary: IDx-DR became the first FDA-authorized system that gives a screening decision without a clinician reading the images. In a 900-person pivotal trial in primary-care clinics it detected more-than-mild diabetic retinopathy with 87.2% sensitivity and 90.7% specificity, beating prespecified targets.

before_after.metric: Sensitivity / specificity vs pre-set trial targets

milestones.why_it_matters: Diabetic eye disease causes preventable blindness. Letting primary-care clinics screen without an eye specialist brings screening to people who rarely see one.

milestones.title: Machine learning plus fast experiments find new metallic-glass systems
milestones.summary: SLAC, Northwestern and NIST researchers trained a model on published data to predict where metallic glasses form, tested it with high-throughput experiments, and retrained on the results. Iterating led to three new glass-forming alloy systems and raised the hit rate from about 1 in 300-400 samples to about 1 in 2-3.

before_after.metric: Share of tested samples that were metallic glasses

milestones.why_it_matters: Metallic glasses are strong, corrosion-resistant alloys that theory predicts poorly. Closing the loop between prediction and experiment lets learning compensate where physics models fall short.

milestones.title: Deep learning identifies wildlife in 3.2 million camera-trap images
milestones.summary: Deep neural networks learned to identify, count and describe 48 species in the 3.2-million-image Snapshot Serengeti set with over 93.8% accuracy. Keeping only confident calls automated 99.3% of images at 96.6% accuracy, matching volunteer crowds and saving over 8.4 years of human labelling.

before_after.metric: Images labelled automatically at volunteer-level accuracy (96.6%)

milestones.why_it_matters: Camera traps gather far more images than experts can label. Automatic species counts turn them into data on animal numbers and behaviour, cheap enough to monitor whole ecosystems.

milestones.title: Machine learning helps ATLAS and CMS observe Higgs decay to bottom quarks
milestones.summary: ATLAS and CMS observed the Higgs boson decaying to bottom-quark pairs, its most common decay but buried under huge backgrounds. Both analyses used machine learning to tag b-quark jets and to separate signal from background. ATLAS reached 5.4 standard deviations and CMS 5.6 (5.5 expected).

before_after.metric: H→bb̄ significance

milestones.why_it_matters: Confirms that the Higgs field gives mass to bottom quarks, as predicted. Shows machine learning can pull rare signals out of overwhelming background, now standard practice in collider physics.

milestones.title: Neural network finds 72 missed pulses from repeating fast radio burst FRB 121102
milestones.summary: Breakthrough Listen researchers trained a convolutional neural network on known bursts and re-searched five hours of Green Bank Telescope data from 26 August 2017. It found 72 pulses the classical search missed, raising the total from 21 to 93, and let the team rule out regular periods longer than about 10 ms.

before_after.metric: FRB 121102 pulses found in the 26 Aug 2017 observation

milestones.why_it_matters: Fast radio bursts are brief and rare. Finding four times more pulses in existing data gives far more evidence about what produces them, without new telescope time.

sources.label: Zhang et al., The Astrophysical Journal 866:149, 2018

milestones.title: AlphaFold wins CASP13 on hard targets: 24 of 43 at TM-score 0.7 or more
milestones.summary: DeepMind's first AlphaFold trained a neural network to predict distances between pairs of amino acids, then optimized a protein shape to fit them. In the blind CASP13 test it ranked first on free-modelling targets, giving high-accuracy structures (TM-score 0.7 or more) for 24 of 43 domains against 14 for the next best method.

before_after.metric: Free-modelling domains at TM-score 0.7 or more (CASP13)

milestones.why_it_matters: Deep learning beat every other CASP13 entry at predicting the shape of hard protein targets, setting up AlphaFold 2 two years later.

sources.label: Senior et al., Proteins, CASP13 system description, 2019-11-11

milestones.title: SpliceAI reads RNA sequence to flag hidden splice-altering mutations
milestones.summary: Illumina's SpliceAI, a deep neural network, predicts splice junctions from transcript sequence and flags noncoding variants that cause cryptic splicing. Predicted splice-altering de novo variants were enriched in autism and intellectual-disability patients and validated in RNA-seq for 21 of 28. The authors estimate 9-11% of pathogenic mutations in rare disorders act this way.
milestones.why_it_matters: Most disease-linked variants sit outside protein-coding sequence and are hard to interpret. Reading splicing from sequence gives geneticists a way to weigh variants that were previously overlooked.

milestones.title: Neural-network forecasts raise value of Google's wind power by about 20%
milestones.summary: A neural network trained on weather forecasts and turbine history predicted output from 700 MW of Google's US wind farms 36 hours ahead, letting Google make hourly delivery commitments to the grid a day in advance. DeepMind reported this raised the value of the wind energy by roughly 20% versus making no time-based commitments.

before_after.metric: value of wind energy

milestones.why_it_matters: Wind output varies, so grids value it less. Reliable day-ahead forecasts make renewables more schedulable and more valuable, easing their integration into power systems.

milestones.title: Deep learning predicts fusion plasma disruptions, including across machines
milestones.summary: The Fusion Recurrent Neural Network, trained on about 2 TB of JET and DIII-D data, warned of disruptions 30 ms ahead. On JET its AUC was 0.952 versus 0.893 for the best classical method; on DIII-D the classical method did slightly better. Trained only on DIII-D, it reached 0.817 on JET versus 0.616.

before_after.metric: disruption-prediction AUC on JET, 30 ms warning

milestones.why_it_matters: Disruptions can damage large reactors like ITER, which cannot afford many training failures. Predictors that transfer from smaller machines help protect bigger ones.

milestones.title: Deep learning forecasts El Niño up to 18 months ahead
milestones.summary: A convolutional neural network, trained first on climate-model simulations and then on 1871-1973 observations, forecast the El Niño/Southern Oscillation with useful skill up to one and a half years ahead. Over 1984-2017 its Niño3.4 correlation skill was much higher than leading dynamical forecast systems, and it predicted the east-west pattern of sea temperatures better.

before_after.metric: Useful ENSO forecast lead time

milestones.why_it_matters: El Niño shifts droughts, floods and harvests worldwide. Several extra months of warning gives farmers, water managers and aid agencies time to prepare.
ai_systems: Convolutional neural network with transfer learning
organizations: Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology

milestones.title: Robot hand trained only in simulation manipulates a Rubik's Cube to solution
milestones.summary: OpenAI trained neural networks for a five-fingered robot hand entirely in simulation, using automatic domain randomization to create ever-harder virtual worlds. In 10 real-world trials its best policy did the equivalent of solving 15-turn scrambles 60% of the time and the hardest 26-turn scrambles 20%. A standard non-learned solver chose the moves.
milestones.why_it_matters: Learning in simulation and transferring to messy reality is how robots could gain dexterous lab and factory skills without years of trial and error on physical hardware.

milestones.title: AI-designed living machines built from frog cells (xenobots)
milestones.summary: An evolutionary algorithm searched simulated body plans made of passive skin and contracting heart-muscle units for designs that move. Biologists then built the best design from Xenopus frog cells. The six organisms built moved in the direction the simulation predicted, and upside-down versions moved much less, as predicted.
milestones.why_it_matters: Computers designed a new kind of living machine, not just a robot, opening a route to custom biological machines for medicine or environmental cleanup.
ai_systems: Evolutionary algorithm in a physics simulator

milestones.title: First AI-designed drug candidate (DSP-1181) enters human trials
milestones.summary: Sumitomo Dainippon Pharma and Exscientia began a phase 1 trial in Japan of DSP-1181, a long-acting serotonin 5-HT1A agonist for obsessive-compulsive disorder. They said AI-assisted design finished the exploratory phase in under 12 months versus a typical 4.5 years. No efficacy data were released, and the drug was discontinued after phase 1.

before_after.metric: Exploratory research phase (company figures)

milestones.why_it_matters: Marked the start of AI-designed molecules being tested in people. Its later discontinuation is a reminder that faster design does not guarantee a drug that works.

milestones.title: AI knowledge graph flags baricitinib for COVID-19; later trials confirm benefit
milestones.summary: In early February 2020, BenevolentAI used its biomedical knowledge graph to propose baricitinib, an approved arthritis drug, against COVID-19. Large randomized trials later confirmed benefit: in RECOVERY (8,156 hospitalized patients) 28-day deaths fell from 14% to 12%, a 13% proportional reduction.

before_after.metric: 28-day mortality, hospitalized COVID-19 (RECOVERY)

milestones.why_it_matters: Shows machine-assisted literature mining can point to an existing, safe drug within days of a new disease, with randomized trials then doing the confirming.

milestones.title: Closed-loop ML finds long-life battery fast-charging protocols in 16 days
milestones.summary: Researchers paired a model that predicts battery lifetime from early cycles (9.1% error using the first 100 cycles, 2019) with Bayesian optimization to search 224 six-step, ten-minute fast-charging protocols. It identified high-cycle-life protocols in 16 days, versus over 500 days for exhaustive testing without early prediction.

before_after.metric: time to optimize 224 fast-charging protocols

milestones.why_it_matters: Battery tests take months because cells must wear out. Predicting lifetime early and choosing experiments smartly can cut years from energy-storage development.

milestones.title: Deep learning finds halicin, an antibiotic unlike known antibiotic classes
milestones.summary: A neural network trained to predict antibacterial activity picked halicin from a drug-repurposing library. It killed a broad range of pathogens, including carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae, and treated pan-resistant A. baumannii and C. difficile infections in mice. Screening over 107 million virtual molecules, 8 of 23 tested predictions were antibacterial.
milestones.why_it_matters: New antibiotic classes are rare while resistance spreads. A model that searches chemical space far faster than wet-lab screening opens a new route to discovery.

milestones.title: AI Feynman recovers all 100 Feynman Lectures equations from data
milestones.summary: MIT's AI Feynman combined neural-network fitting with physics-inspired tricks (symmetry, separability and dimensional analysis) to find formulas from data. Given data sampled from the 100 equations in the Feynman Lectures on Physics, it recovered all of them, where prior public software found 71, and raised success on a harder set from 15% to 90%.

before_after.metric: Feynman Lectures equations recovered from data

milestones.why_it_matters: Physics advances by finding compact laws behind data. Automating that step could help find formulas in new data where humans have no starting guess.

milestones.title: Real-time AI polyp detection raises adenoma detection in colonoscopy trial
milestones.summary: In a 685-patient randomized trial at three Italian centres, the GI Genius system drawing boxes around suspected lesions in real time raised the adenoma detection rate from 40.4% to 54.8%, with more adenomas per colonoscopy and no longer withdrawal time.

before_after.metric: Adenoma detection rate

milestones.why_it_matters: About a quarter of precancerous colon growths are missed at colonoscopy. Catching more could prevent cancers, if the gain lasts and doctors keep their own skills.
milestones.contested_note: The trial result itself is not disputed, but Budzyń et al. (Lancet Gastroenterology & Hepatology, 2025; observational, four Polish centres) found endoscopists' adenoma detection without AI fell from 28.4% to 22.4% after routine AI use, suggesting deskilling.

milestones.title: Active learning finds Cu-Al catalyst that turns CO2 into ethylene efficiently
milestones.summary: Toronto and Carnegie Mellon researchers screened copper-containing alloys with density functional theory guided by active machine learning, singling out copper-aluminium. The resulting electrocatalyst reduced CO2 to ethylene with over 80% Faradaic efficiency at 400 mA/cm², versus about 66% for pure copper, the highest efficiency reported at the time.

before_after.metric: Faradaic efficiency, CO2 to ethylene

milestones.why_it_matters: Turning captured CO2 into plastic feedstock with renewable electricity needs efficient catalysts. Machine-learning-guided searches of alloy surfaces find candidates faster than trial and error.
ai_systems: Active machine-learning surrogate model with DFT

milestones.title: Mobile robot chemist runs 688 experiments in 8 days to improve a photocatalyst
milestones.summary: A free-roaming robot at the University of Liverpool, steered by a batched Bayesian search algorithm, worked autonomously for eight days and performed 688 experiments across a ten-variable space. It found photocatalyst mixtures for producing hydrogen from water that were six times more active than the starting formulations.

before_after.metric: Hydrogen-evolution activity of photocatalyst mixture

milestones.why_it_matters: Instead of rebuilding labs around machines, the robot used ordinary instruments the way a human researcher would, pointing to self-driving labs that work day and night.

milestones.title: Earthquake Transformer detects twice as many quakes with a third of the stations
milestones.summary: An attention-based deep network detects earthquakes and picks P- and S-wave arrival times together, close to human analyst precision. Applied to five weeks of continuous data from the 2000 Tottori earthquake sequence in Japan, it detected and located twice as many earthquakes while using fewer than a third of the seismic stations.

before_after.metric: Earthquakes detected and located (Tottori 2000 sequence)

milestones.why_it_matters: Small earthquakes outline the faults that make big ones. Catalogues with many more small events give a sharper picture of where stress builds up.

milestones.title: Janelia and Google map about 25,000 neurons of the fly central brain
milestones.summary: Janelia and Google reconstructed the central brain of a fruit fly from electron-microscope images, using flood-filling neural networks plus over 50 person-years of human proofreading. The open map holds about 25,000 neurons and about 20 million chemical synapses, then the largest dense reconstruction to date.
milestones.why_it_matters: A full wiring map lets scientists trace how circuits produce behaviour such as navigation, sleep and learning, rather than infer it from isolated recordings.

milestones.title: Synthesis-planning software designs working routes to complex natural products
milestones.summary: Grzybowski's group augmented Chematica's reaction knowledge and AI routines with causal, multistep strategy so it could plan routes to complex natural products. In a Turing-like test, synthesis experts largely could not tell its routes from human-designed ones, and three computer-designed natural-product syntheses were validated in the laboratory.
milestones.why_it_matters: Natural products demand far-sighted, many-step plans with few precedents to copy. Showing software can strategize at that level suggests expert-level automated planning is feasible.
organizations: UNIST / IBS Center for Soft and Living Matter

milestones.title: Deep learning counts 1.8 billion trees in the West African Sahara and Sahel
milestones.summary: Deep learning applied to sub-metre satellite images mapped the crown of every tree larger than 3 square metres across 1.3 million square kilometres of West Africa. It found over 1.8 billion trees, 13.4 per hectare on average, with surprisingly high density even in deserts, challenging common narratives of dryland desertification.

before_after.metric: Individual trees mapped outside forests in the region

milestones.why_it_matters: Scattered trees store carbon and support people and wildlife, yet were invisible in forest statistics. Counting them one by one changes how drylands are monitored and managed.

milestones.title: AlphaFold 2 reaches near-experimental accuracy at CASP14
milestones.summary: In the blind CASP14 test DeepMind's AlphaFold 2 reached a median 92.4 GDT across all targets (87.0 on the hardest), with average error near 1.6 angstroms. The 2021 Nature paper reports median backbone error of 0.96 Å against 2.8 Å for the next-best method; a carbon atom is about 1.4 Å wide.

before_after.metric: Median backbone error at CASP14 (r.m.s.d. at 95% coverage)

milestones.why_it_matters: Protein shape sets function, but each lab-solved structure took months or years. A predictor near lab accuracy puts structures within reach for almost any protein sequence.

milestones.title: Machine-learned inlining and register-allocation policies ship in LLVM
milestones.summary: Google's MLGO framework put trained models directly into LLVM, the compiler behind much of today's software. A learned inlining policy shrank code 3-7% beyond LLVM's -Oz setting (6.3% on Fuchsia), and a learned register-allocation policy raised datacenter throughput 0.3-1.5%. Both are in LLVM and deployed in production.

before_after.metric: Binary size vs LLVM -Oz

milestones.why_it_matters: Compilers apply hand-tuned rules to every program they build. Learning those rules from data yields savings that multiply across all the software compiled with them.

milestones.title: BirdNET neural network identifies 984 bird species by sound
milestones.summary: Cornell and Chemnitz researchers trained a 27-million-parameter ResNet to name 984 North American and European bird species from audio. It scored mean average precision 0.791 on single-species recordings but F0.5 0.414 on annotated soundscapes, showing field audio remains much harder.
milestones.why_it_matters: Bird counts track environmental change, but expert surveys cover little ground. Automatic sound identification lets recorders monitor continuously, although accuracy in noisy field audio is still limited.

sources.label: Kahl et al., Ecological Informatics 61:101236, online 2021-01-27

milestones.title: Ramanujan Machine algorithms conjecture new formulas for fundamental constants
milestones.summary: Technion researchers built algorithms that match numerical values to propose continued-fraction formulas, finding dozens of known and previously unknown representations of π, e, Catalan's constant and values of the Riemann zeta function. The outputs are conjectures: the algorithms supply no proofs. Published in Nature after a 2019 preprint.
milestones.why_it_matters: Turns formula-guessing, historically the gift of rare intuitions like Ramanujan's, into systematic computer search that hands mathematicians precise statements to prove.

milestones.title: Volunteers and Bayesian neural networks measure shapes of 314,000 galaxies
milestones.summary: Galaxy Zoo volunteers gave 7.5 million classifications of DECaLS images, with active learning steering them to the most useful galaxies. An ensemble of Bayesian convolutional networks trained on those labels then measured detailed morphology (bars, spiral arms, tidal features) with uncertainties for all 314,000 galaxies, about 99% accurate against confident volunteer answers.

before_after.metric: Galaxies with detailed morphology measurements

milestones.why_it_matters: Galaxy shapes record how galaxies formed and merged. Combining people and models lets surveys of hundreds of millions of galaxies get careful classifications that people alone could never finish.

milestones.title: WHO recommends AI chest X-ray reading for tuberculosis screening
milestones.summary: WHO's 2021 TB screening guideline conditionally recommended computer-aided detection software in place of human readers of digital chest X-rays for people aged 15 and over, followed by confirmatory testing. A 2025 independent evaluation found six CAD products meeting WHO performance standards.
milestones.why_it_matters: Many countries with heavy TB burdens have few radiologists. Software that reads X-rays lets screening programs reach remote and poor communities.
ai_systems: Computer-aided detection (CAD) software for chest X-ray

sources.label: WHO consolidated TB guidelines, module 2: screening, 2021-03-22
WHO policy statement on CAD for TB screening, 2025-06-10

milestones.title: Reinforcement learning finds counterexamples to combinatorics conjectures
milestones.summary: Adam Zsolt Wagner used the deep cross-entropy method, a simple reinforcement-learning algorithm, to build graphs and matrices that refute several open conjectures about adjacency and distance eigenvalues of graphs, and a question of Brualdi and Cao on permanents of pattern-avoiding matrices. Each conjecture needed only a score function to reward violations.
milestones.why_it_matters: A cheap, general recipe, rewarding a network for breaking a conjecture, let machines hunt counterexamples; it was later extended in PatternBoost and AlphaEvolve.

milestones.title: AI-read ECGs raise detection of weak heart pumping in a randomized trial
milestones.summary: In a pragmatic trial of 120 Mayo Clinic primary-care teams (22,641 adults), giving clinicians an AI-ECG alert for low ejection fraction raised new diagnoses within 90 days from 1.6% to 2.1%; among AI-positive patients, from 14.5% to 19.5%.

before_after.metric: New low-ejection-fraction diagnoses within 90 days

milestones.why_it_matters: A cheap, routine test read by AI can uncover hidden, treatable heart failure earlier, showing AI can change real clinical decisions rather than only scoring well on old data.

milestones.title: Reinforcement learning lays out chip floorplans used in Google TPUs
milestones.summary: A deep reinforcement learning agent placed large circuit blocks on chip floorplans in under six hours, matching or beating human experts on power, timing and area by Google's account, against weeks or months of manual work. Google says the method, later named AlphaChip, was used in TPU v5e, v5p and Trillium.

before_after.metric: Time to produce a chip floorplan
before_after.before: Weeks to months of expert effort

milestones.why_it_matters: Chip layout is slow expert labour. If AI can do it well, better hardware arrives sooner, and that hardware in turn trains better AI.
milestones.contested_note: Independent reassessments (Cheng, Kahng et al., ISPD 2023, updated in IEEE TCAD; arXiv 2302.11014) and a meta-analysis by Igor Markov (Communications of the ACM, 2024) found the method trailing simulated annealing and commercial tools. Nature attached an editor's note in September 2023 and removed it with an addendum in September 2024; Google's rebuttal (arXiv 2411.10053) defends the results.

milestones.title: RoseTTAFold, a three-track network, nears AlphaFold 2 accuracy
milestones.summary: The Baker lab's RoseTTAFold passes information between sequence, distance-map and 3D-coordinate levels, reaching accuracy approaching DeepMind's CASP14 results. After a 1.5-hour sequence search it predicts a backbone for proteins under 400 residues in about 10 minutes on one GPU, and builds protein-complex models from sequence alone.
milestones.why_it_matters: Gave academic labs a fast, openly available structure predictor; the same network was later fine-tuned into RFdiffusion for protein design.
organizations: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design

milestones.title: Generative model of radar gives rain forecasts experts prefer 89% of the time
milestones.summary: A deep generative model of radar data forecasts rainfall 5-90 minutes ahead over areas up to 1,536 x 1,280 km without the blurring of earlier deep learning methods. In a systematic evaluation by more than 50 expert meteorologists it ranked first for accuracy and usefulness in 89% of cases against two competing methods.

before_after.metric: Expert meteorologists' first choice vs two competing methods

milestones.why_it_matters: Short-term rain forecasts decide flood warnings, flights and outdoor work. Sharper predictions of heavy rain in the next hour or two directly reduce risk.

milestones.title: ExoMiner deep learning model validates 301 new Kepler exoplanets
milestones.summary: NASA Ames built ExoMiner, a deep network that mirrors the tests human vetters use, and ran it on the Kepler archive. It statistically validated 301 new exoplanets. At 99% precision it recovered 93.6% of planets in the test set, against 76.3% for the best earlier classifier. A 2023 extension added 69 more, for 370.

before_after.metric: Recall at 99% precision on Kepler test set

milestones.why_it_matters: Each validated planet adds to the census used to estimate how common worlds like Earth are. A trustworthy, explainable classifier turns a backlog of ambiguous signals into planets.

sources.label: Valizadegan et al., The Astrophysical Journal 926:120, 2022 (arXiv 2021-11-19)
Valizadegan et al., 69 more planets via multiplicity boost, The Astronomical Journal 166:28, 2023

milestones.title: AI-designed shape extends a new kind of self-replication in frog-cell organisms
milestones.summary: Researchers found that frog-cell clusters can reproduce by sweeping loose cells into piles that grow into copies, a form of replication not seen in any organism. An AI search found a C-shaped parent design that raised replication rounds from a mean of 1.2 to 3, reaching four generations, in a small number of lab trials.

before_after.metric: Rounds of self-replication

milestones.why_it_matters: AI design improved a living behaviour humans had only just observed, suggesting computers can steer biology toward useful functions quickly, without genetic engineering.
ai_systems: Evolutionary algorithm in a physics simulator

milestones.title: ML guides mathematicians to new results in knot and representation theory
milestones.summary: DeepMind worked with mathematicians at Oxford and Sydney, using neural networks and attribution techniques to spot patterns between mathematical objects. This produced a new theorem linking a knot's algebraic signature to its geometric slope, and a candidate algorithm toward the combinatorial invariance conjecture for symmetric groups.
milestones.why_it_matters: A high-profile demonstration that machine learning can point professional mathematicians toward new conjectures and theorems in pure mathematics, not only compute examples.
ai_systems: Supervised neural networks with saliency attribution
milestones.contested_note: Ernest Davis (NYU) argued the AI role was overstated: small in the knot result, and in the representation-theory result not very different in kind from decades of experimental mathematics (arXiv:2112.04324).

milestones.title: Reinforcement learning designs smaller adder circuits used in NVIDIA Hopper GPUs
milestones.summary: NVIDIA's PrefixRL agent designed parallel prefix circuits such as adders from scratch, with synthesis tools in the loop. Its best 64-bit adder had 25% lower area than a commercial EDA tool's adder at the same delay. NVIDIA says its Hopper GPU architecture contains nearly 13,000 instances of AI-designed circuits.

before_after.metric: 64-bit adder area at equal delay

milestones.why_it_matters: Adders sit in every processor, repeated thousands of times. Smaller and faster arithmetic blocks mean chips that need less silicon and power.

milestones.title: AlphaCode writes programs at median human level in coding contests
milestones.summary: DeepMind's AlphaCode sampled very many candidate programs from a language model, filtered them by running them on example tests, and submitted the best. In 10 simulated Codeforces contests with over 5,000 participants each, it ranked on average in the top 54.3%, roughly median human level, a first for an AI system.

before_after.metric: Average Codeforces contest ranking
before_after.before: Earlier AI systems solved few contest problems

milestones.why_it_matters: Contest problems demand reasoning about algorithms, not just translating instructions into code. This showed language models could begin to solve programming problems they had never seen.

milestones.title: MuZero learns video compression control used on YouTube traffic
milestones.summary: DeepMind applied MuZero, a game-playing reinforcement learning agent, to choose quantization settings in the open-source VP9 encoder. In tests it cut compressed video size by 6.28% at equal quality versus libvpx's two-pass rate control; on part of YouTube's live traffic it reduced bitrate by 4% on average.

before_after.metric: Bitrate at the same video quality
before_after.after: 6.28% smaller in tests; 4% average on YouTube traffic

milestones.why_it_matters: Video makes up most internet traffic. A few percent less data per video saves bandwidth, energy and cost for billions of viewers, especially on slow connections.

milestones.title: Reinforcement learning controls and shapes fusion plasma in the TCV tokamak
milestones.summary: DeepMind and EPFL trained a deep reinforcement-learning controller in simulation, then ran it on the TCV tokamak, commanding the full set of 19 magnetic coils directly. It created and held elongated, negative-triangularity and 'snowflake' plasmas, and sustained two separate plasma 'droplets' at once, cutting the design effort for new configurations.

before_after.metric: controller for a new plasma shape
before_after.before: many hand-designed feedback loops, re-engineered per configuration
before_after.after: one learned controller specified by high-level goals

milestones.why_it_matters: Fusion power needs hot plasma held in precise shapes. Learned controllers make it far cheaper to explore new, possibly better, plasma shapes for future reactors.

milestones.title: FourCastNet produces a week-long global forecast in under two seconds
milestones.summary: FourCastNet, a Fourier neural operator model trained on reanalysis data, produced global 0.25-degree forecasts matching ECMWF's IFS at short lead times for large-scale variables and beating it on fine-scale variables such as precipitation. A week-long forecast took under two seconds, orders of magnitude faster than the physics-based model.

before_after.metric: Time for a week-long global 0.25-degree forecast

milestones.why_it_matters: Cheap forecasts allow thousands of ensemble members, giving better odds for rare extreme events. It was one of the first signs that learned models could rival physics-based forecasting.

milestones.title: Machine-learning-guided enzyme breaks down PET from 51 waste products in a week
milestones.summary: UT Austin researchers used MutCompute, a structure-based neural network, to propose mutations to a plastic-degrading enzyme. FAST-PETase, with three predicted mutations plus two from an earlier variant, almost completely degraded untreated post-consumer PET from 51 different products within one week, worked between 30 and 50 °C, and enabled closed-loop recycling.
milestones.why_it_matters: PET is about 12% of global solid waste. Enzymes that digest untreated plastic at mild temperatures could make recycling greener, though industrial use needs much faster rates.
milestones.contested_note: Arnal et al. (ACS Catalysis, 2023-09-26) compared four engineered PET enzymes under standardized, larger-scale conditions and found FAST-PETase's low depolymerization rate may rule out industrial use; LCC-ICCG converted 98% of PET in 24 hours.

milestones.title: Deployed AI sepsis alert linked to fewer deaths across five hospitals
milestones.summary: TREWS monitored 590,736 patients at five hospitals. Among 6,877 septic patients flagged before antibiotics, those whose alert a clinician confirmed within 3 hours had in-hospital mortality 3.3 points lower (18.7% relative) after adjustment. The study was observational, not randomized.
milestones.why_it_matters: Sepsis kills quickly and hides early. An alert that clinicians trust and act on could save many lives, but proving it needs randomized trials.
milestones.contested_note: Nemati et al. (UC San Diego; medRxiv preprint, 2022-08-09) argued the confirmed-vs-unconfirmed comparison is biased by unadjusted process-of-care confounding; the TREWS authors replied (medRxiv, 2022-09-17) that adjusting for such variables does not change their conclusions.

milestones.title: AlphaFold database grows from under a million to 214 million structures
milestones.summary: In July 2022 DeepMind and EMBL-EBI expanded the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database to 214,684,311 predicted structures, covering almost all of UniProt across plants, bacteria, animals and other organisms. The previous release, in December 2021, held 992,316 models. The structures are free to use.

before_after.metric: Predicted structures in the AlphaFold database

milestones.why_it_matters: Instead of waiting for lab work, biologists can look up a predicted structure for nearly any catalogued protein, at no cost.

sources.label: EMBL-EBI blog on the new release (exact counts)
Varadi et al., Nucleic Acids Research, AlphaFold DB in 2024, 2023-11-02

milestones.title: ProteinMPNN designs sequences that rescue previously failed protein designs
milestones.summary: ProteinMPNN, a message-passing neural network, designs amino-acid sequences for a given protein backbone. On native backbones it recovered 52.4% of residues against 32.9% for Rosetta. X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM and function tests showed it rescued earlier Rosetta- or AlphaFold-made designs that had failed.

before_after.metric: Native sequence recovery on native backbones

milestones.why_it_matters: Choosing amino acids that fold into a chosen shape is the second half of protein design. A faster, more reliable tool makes new proteins easier to make and test.
organizations: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design

milestones.title: AlphaTensor finds faster matrix multiplication algorithms
milestones.summary: DeepMind turned the search for matrix multiplication algorithms into a single-player game for an AlphaZero-style agent. AlphaTensor found a way to multiply 4x4 matrices in mod-2 arithmetic with 47 multiplications instead of 49, the first improvement on Strassen's two-level method in 50 years, and improved best-known counts for several other sizes.

before_after.metric: Multiplications for 4x4 matrices (mod 2)

milestones.why_it_matters: Matrix multiplication is the core operation of graphics, simulation and AI. Showing machines can find provably correct algorithms that humans missed changed how algorithm research is done.

milestones.title: Active learning finds two high-entropy Invar alloys with very low expansion
milestones.summary: Max Planck researchers combined machine learning, density functional theory, thermodynamic calculations and experiments in a closed active-learning loop. After making just 17 new alloys out of millions of possible compositions, they identified two high-entropy Invar alloys with extremely low thermal expansion, around 2×10⁻⁶ per kelvin at 300 K.

before_after.metric: Alloys synthesized to find low-expansion hits

milestones.why_it_matters: Materials that barely expand with heat are vital for precision instruments and gas transport. Finding them in a nearly infinite composition space with few experiments shows how learning cuts search cost.

milestones.title: AlphaFold structure used to find a drug hit for a target with no lab structure
milestones.summary: Insilico combined target-ranking (PandaOmics) and generative chemistry (Chemistry42) with an AlphaFold-predicted structure of CDK20, a liver-cancer target lacking an experimental structure. A hit (Kd 9.2 µM) came within 30 days of target selection after synthesizing 7 compounds; a second round gave ISM042-2-048 (IC50 33.4 nM).
milestones.why_it_matters: Most disease proteins lack lab-solved structures. Designing drugs on predicted structures widens the set of targets drug hunters can attack.

milestones.title: Deep learning search of 820 stars turns up eight new SETI signals of interest
milestones.summary: A semi-unsupervised variational autoencoder searched 480 hours of Green Bank Telescope data on 820 nearby stars from Breakthrough Listen. It cut candidate signals by about two orders of magnitude versus earlier analyses of the same data and flagged eight signals of interest not found before. Re-observations have not detected them again.
milestones.why_it_matters: Radio searches for technology elsewhere drown in human-made interference. A model that filters it well makes it practical to search many more stars with the same effort.

milestones.title: Deep learning designs working luciferase enzymes from scratch
milestones.summary: University of Washington researchers used deep-learning 'family-wide hallucination' to generate idealized protein scaffolds with varied pockets, then designed artificial luciferases from scratch. The best, a 13.9 kDa enzyme stable above 95 °C, has catalytic efficiency near 10^6 per molar per second on diphenylterazine, comparable to natural luciferases but far more specific.
milestones.why_it_matters: Building enzymes from scratch, rather than editing natural ones, opens catalysts for reactions nature never evolved. The authors point to broad biomedical applications.
organizations: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design

milestones.title: Professional Go players make better, more novel moves after AlphaGo
milestones.summary: Using the superhuman Go program KataGo to score 5.8 million moves by professional players from 1950 to 2021, researchers found decision quality rose significantly after superhuman AI appeared in 2016-17, after 66 years of little change. Never-before-played moves became more frequent and were linked to better decisions.
milestones.why_it_matters: Evidence that superhuman AI can raise human expertise rather than replace it: people learned new ideas from the machine and broke away from inherited habits.
ai_systems: AlphaGo and later superhuman Go programs (source of new ideas)

milestones.title: ESMFold builds an atlas of 617 million metagenomic protein structures
milestones.summary: Meta AI's protein language model, scaled to 15 billion parameters, predicts atomic-level structure directly from a single sequence, about ten times faster than earlier high-resolution methods. It built the ESM Metagenomic Atlas of more than 617 million predicted structures, over 225 million of them high confidence.
milestones.why_it_matters: Most proteins in nature come from microbes never grown in a lab. A fast, alignment-free predictor lets researchers survey that unseen diversity at scale.

milestones.title: AI beats sonographers at first-pass heart-function reading in blinded trial
milestones.summary: In the first blinded randomized trial of AI in echocardiography (3,495 studies), cardiologists substantially changed the AI's initial ejection-fraction estimate in 16.8% of studies versus 27.2% for sonographers, and could not tell which source they were reviewing. The AI workflow also saved time.

before_after.metric: Initial assessments substantially changed by cardiologist (>5% LVEF)

milestones.why_it_matters: Heart-pumping measurements drive many treatment decisions. A blinded randomized trial is the gold-standard test that AI helps in practice, not just on benchmarks.

milestones.title: Machine learning sharpens the image of the M87* black hole
milestones.summary: PRIMO, a dictionary-learning method trained on over 30,000 simulated black hole images, re-analysed the 2017 Event Horizon Telescope data of M87*. The authors report reaching the array's full resolution for the first time, with the ring about half as wide as in 2019. Gaps are filled using those simulations.

before_after.metric: Width of the M87* ring in the reconstructed image

milestones.why_it_matters: A sharper ring gives tighter measurements of the black hole's mass and a cleaner test of Einstein's gravity, using data already collected.

milestones.title: Deep learning finds abaucin, a narrow-spectrum antibiotic for A. baumannii
milestones.summary: Researchers screened ~7,500 molecules against Acinetobacter baumannii, a multidrug-resistant hospital pathogen, trained a neural network on the results and predicted new actives. They found abaucin, which targets A. baumannii narrowly, disrupts lipoprotein trafficking via LolE, and controlled infection in a mouse wound model.
milestones.why_it_matters: Narrow-spectrum drugs spare helpful bacteria and slow resistance. AI made it practical to find one against a pathogen that resists most existing antibiotics.

milestones.title: Geneformer, pretrained on 30 million cells, predicts gene-network behaviour
milestones.summary: Geneformer, pretrained on about 30 million single-cell transcriptomes, learned gene-network structure without labels. With little extra data it improved predictions across chromatin and network tasks, and in cardiomyopathy disease modelling it flagged candidate therapeutic targets.
milestones.why_it_matters: Mapping gene networks usually needs huge datasets. A pretrained model that works with little data could help study rare diseases and tissues that are hard to sample.
milestones.contested_note: Kedzierska et al. (Genome Biology, 2025-04-18) tested Geneformer and scGPT with no fine-tuning (zero-shot) and found that in some cases simpler methods could outperform them. The Nature paper's gains rest on fine-tuning, so the critique limits, rather than overturns, its claims.

milestones.title: AlphaDev discovers faster sorting routines now in the LLVM C++ library
milestones.summary: DeepMind's AlphaDev searched over assembly instructions and found shorter routines for sorting three to five items. Merged into LLVM's libc++ sort, they ran up to 70% faster on short sequences and about 1.7% faster beyond 250,000 elements. A hashing routine it found, released in Abseil, was 30% faster for 9-16 byte inputs.

before_after.metric: libc++ sort speed on short (3-5 element) sequences

milestones.why_it_matters: Sorting and hashing run trillions of times a day. Small gains in these shared library routines save time and energy across all the software that calls them.

milestones.title: Machine learning helps IceCube detect high-energy neutrinos from the Milky Way
milestones.summary: The IceCube Collaboration applied machine-learning techniques to select and reconstruct neutrino events in 10 years of data from its Antarctic detector. Comparing models of diffuse galactic emission with background, it identified neutrino emission from the plane of the Milky Way at 4.5 standard deviations.

before_after.metric: Galactic-plane neutrino emission

milestones.why_it_matters: Neutrinos fly straight from where cosmic rays are made, so seeing them from our galaxy helps locate cosmic-ray sources. Machine learning separated the faint signal from background.

milestones.title: Pangu-Weather beats ECMWF's operational forecast in reanalysis-based tests
milestones.summary: Huawei's Pangu-Weather, 3D neural networks trained on 39 years of global reanalysis data, gave more accurate deterministic medium-range forecasts than ECMWF's operational IFS on all tested variables when both started from reanalysis data, and tracked tropical cyclones more accurately than ECMWF-HRES. The authors called it the first AI method to do so.

before_after.metric: Deterministic medium-range skill vs ECMWF IFS (reanalysis-initialised)

milestones.why_it_matters: For decades the best forecasts came from solving physics equations on supercomputers. This showed a model learned from past weather could match them, opening the door to operational AI forecasting.

milestones.title: RFdiffusion generates new protein binders, assemblies and active sites
milestones.summary: Fine-tuning the RoseTTAFold structure network as a diffusion model gave a general generator of protein backbones, used for binders, symmetric assemblies, metal-binding proteins and enzyme active sites. Hundreds of designs were tested experimentally, and a cryo-EM structure of a designed binder matched its design model nearly exactly.
milestones.why_it_matters: One general protein generator can replace bespoke design pipelines: specify a function such as binding a target and get candidate proteins to test.
organizations: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design

milestones.title: Language model clears the pass mark on US medical licensing-style questions
milestones.summary: Google's Flan-PaLM scored 67.6% on MedQA US licensing-exam-style questions, above the roughly 60% pass mark and more than 17% above the prior best. Instruction-tuned Med-PaLM improved clinician-rated answers but remained inferior to clinicians. Preprinted December 2022.

before_after.metric: Accuracy on MedQA (USMLE-style questions)

milestones.why_it_matters: Marked the point where general language models began holding usable medical knowledge, starting serious testing of them on real clinical tasks. Exam scores are not patient outcomes.

milestones.title: Graph neural network helps CMS exclude zero HHVV coupling at 6.3 sigma
milestones.summary: CMS searched for pairs of high-energy Higgs bosons decaying to bottom quarks, identifying them with the ParticleNet graph neural network, which raised selection efficiency by about 50% over the previous tagger. The analysis excluded a vanishing coupling of two Higgs to two vector bosons (κ2V = 0) for the first time, at 6.3 standard deviations.

before_after.metric: H→bb̄ jet selection efficiency at similar background rejection

milestones.why_it_matters: How Higgs bosons pair with W and Z bosons tests whether the Higgs keeps high-energy collisions well-behaved. Better AI tagging extracts such tests from limited collision data.

milestones.title: Autonomous drone Swift beats human world champions in real races
milestones.summary: Swift, a racing drone trained with deep reinforcement learning in simulation and corrected with real flight data, raced head-to-head against three champion human pilots on a fixed track using only onboard sensors. It won 15 of 25 races and set the fastest recorded race time, half a second ahead of the best human.

before_after.metric: Head-to-head races against champion human pilots
before_after.before: No autonomous drone had matched champion pilots
before_after.after: Won 15 of 25 races; fastest time by 0.5 s

milestones.why_it_matters: The first time an AI-controlled robot beat human champions in a competitive physical sport, showing learned control can work at the limits of real hardware with noisy sensing.

milestones.title: AlphaMissense rates all 71 million possible missense variants
milestones.summary: AlphaMissense, AlphaFold fine-tuned on human and primate variant frequencies, rated all 71 million possible human missense variants. At a threshold giving 90% precision on known disease variants it classified 89%: 57% likely benign, 32% likely pathogenic. Only about 0.1% of all possible variants had been confirmed by human experts.
milestones.why_it_matters: Most human missense variants have unknown clinical meaning. Proteome-wide predictions give geneticists a starting point for ranking which rare changes may cause disease.
milestones.contested_note: An independent rare-disease cohort study (npj Genomic Medicine, 2025-02-28) found AlphaMissense precision of 32.9% and recall of 57.6% for expert-curated pathogenic variants, and poor performance in intrinsically disordered regions. The 90% precision figure is from the developers' own known-variant set.

sources.label: Rare-disease cohort evaluation, npj Genomic Medicine, 2025-02-28

milestones.title: AI designs a walking robot from scratch in under 30 seconds on a laptop
milestones.summary: Researchers replaced slow evolutionary search, which needed days of supercomputing, with a gradient-based method that shaped a robot body starting from a random legless blob. In under 30 seconds and about ten attempts on a laptop it consistently invented legs. The manufactured robot walked significantly farther than an unoptimized one.

before_after.metric: Time to design a working robot body

milestones.why_it_matters: Near-instant automated design makes it practical to invent custom machines on demand for medical, environmental or space tasks.

milestones.title: First supernova found, confirmed, classified and reported without humans
milestones.summary: BTSbot, a neural network scanning Zwicky Transient Facility alerts, flagged SN 2023tyk, requested a spectrum from a robotic telescope at Palomar, and the SNIascore model classified it as Type Ia. It was reported publicly on 7 October 2023 with no human step. People had spent about 2,200 hours over six years on such scanning.

before_after.metric: Human steps from detection to public classification

milestones.why_it_matters: New surveys will find millions of changing objects each night. Closing the loop automatically frees astronomers to study the events instead of sorting them.

sources.label: Rehemtulla et al., The Astrophysical Journal 972, 2024 (arXiv:2401.15167)

milestones.title: GPT-4 guides chemists to a new series of metal-organic frameworks
milestones.summary: Omar Yaghi's UC Berkeley group used GPT-4 in a loop: it proposed synthesis steps, a human ran the experiments and reported successes and failures, and it adjusted. This guided the discovery of four isoreticular MOFs (the MOF-521 series); one had been made by accident before but never published, and GPT-4 was not told how.
milestones.why_it_matters: Metal-organic frameworks can capture carbon dioxide and harvest water from air. A language model steering their synthesis in plain language lowers the skill barrier to making new porous materials.

milestones.title: Robotic AI chemist makes oxygen-evolution catalyst from Martian meteorites
milestones.summary: A robotic AI chemist at USTC pretreated Martian meteorite material, synthesized, characterized and tested oxygen-evolution catalysts, and used a machine-learning model built from simulations and measurements to pick the best formula among more than three million possible compositions, without human intervention. The catalyst ran over 550,000 seconds at 10 mA/cm².
milestones.why_it_matters: Making oxygen from local rock would ease crewed missions to Mars. Fully automated catalyst discovery is also what remote, unstaffed laboratories would need.
ai_systems: Robotic AI-Chemist (machine-learning model with Bayesian optimization)
organizations: University of Science and Technology of China

milestones.title: GraphCast beats the leading deterministic forecast on 90% of targets
milestones.summary: GraphCast, a graph neural network trained on four decades of ERA5 reanalysis, forecasts hundreds of variables globally at 0.25 degrees for 10 days in under a minute. It outperformed the most accurate operational deterministic systems on 90% of 1,380 verification targets and better supported prediction of tropical cyclones, atmospheric rivers and extreme temperatures.

before_after.metric: Verification targets where GraphCast beats ECMWF HRES

milestones.why_it_matters: A 10-day global forecast on one machine in a minute makes top-quality forecasting cheap enough for any weather service. NOAA later built its operational AI model on it.

sources.label: Lam et al., Science 382:1416, published online 2023-11-14

milestones.title: A-Lab robot autonomously synthesizes computer-predicted inorganic compounds
milestones.summary: Berkeley Lab's A-Lab used robotics, literature-trained recipe models and active learning to make computer-predicted inorganic powders. Over 17 days it first reported making 41 of 58 targets. A January 2026 correction, after manual re-analysis of X-ray data, reports 36 of 57 and says the compounds were new to the platform, not to science.
milestones.why_it_matters: Predicting materials is now far faster than making them. A robot that plans, makes and analyzes solid-state syntheses could close that gap, if its automated analysis can be trusted.
ai_systems: A-Lab (recipe models, active learning, ML X-ray analysis)
milestones.contested_note: Leeman, Schoop, Palgrave et al. (PRX Energy, 2024-03-07) argued no new materials were made: automated X-ray analysis was unreliable and about two thirds of claimed products were likely known disordered phases. Nature's Author Correction (2026-01-19) revised the novelty wording and cut the success count to 36.

milestones.title: GNoME predicts 2.2 million new inorganic crystals, about 380,000 stable
milestones.summary: Google DeepMind's GNoME graph networks, trained at scale with active learning and DFT, found 2.2 million structures below the previously known stability hull, about 381,000 of them on the updated hull. The authors say this lifts known stable crystals from about 48,000 to 421,000; 736 had already been made independently in labs.

before_after.metric: Known stable inorganic crystals

milestones.why_it_matters: New batteries, chips and solar cells start with new crystals. A far larger computed map of plausibly stable compounds gives experimenters many more starting points.
milestones.contested_note: Cheetham and Seshadri (Chemistry of Materials, 2024-04-08) found 'scant evidence' of compounds that are novel, credible and useful; Leeman et al. (PRX Energy, 2024-03-07) warned such predictions neglect compositional disorder, so many 'new' ordered compounds may be known disordered phases.

milestones.title: FunSearch evolves better online bin-packing heuristics with a language model
milestones.summary: FunSearch pairs a code-writing language model with an automatic evaluator in an evolutionary loop. Alongside its cap-set results in mathematics, it found online bin-packing heuristics that beat first fit and best fit on every benchmark tested, for example 0.68% excess bins versus 3.98% for best fit on Weibull 5k instances.

before_after.metric: Excess bins, Weibull 5k online bin packing

milestones.why_it_matters: Bin packing is how jobs are fitted onto servers and goods into trucks. Readable, machine-written heuristics that waste less space can be inspected and adopted by people.

milestones.title: FunSearch uses a language model to find larger cap sets
milestones.summary: DeepMind paired a pretrained language model with an automatic evaluator to evolve programs. For the cap set problem it found a 512-element cap set in dimension 8 (previous best 496) and raised the lower bound on asymptotic cap set capacity from 2.2180 to 2.2202. The winning programs were readable by mathematicians.

before_after.metric: Largest known cap set in dimension 8

milestones.why_it_matters: Reported as the first time a large language model helped find a verified new result on an established open problem, by writing programs whose outputs a computer checks.

milestones.title: GPT-4-based Coscientist plans and runs chemistry experiments on lab robots
milestones.summary: Carnegie Mellon's Coscientist gave GPT-4 internet and documentation search, code execution and laboratory automation, then had it design, plan and carry out experiments across six human-set tasks. It optimized palladium-catalysed cross-coupling reactions, writing the code that drove lab hardware from plain-language goals; the authors describe it as (semi-)autonomous.
milestones.why_it_matters: It was an early demonstration that a language model could turn a written research goal into working robot instructions and real reaction results, not just text.

milestones.title: Explainable deep learning uncovers a new structural class of antibiotics
milestones.summary: After testing 39,312 compounds and predicting activity and toxicity for 12 million more with graph neural networks, researchers used explainable substructure rationales to pick 283 to test. One new structural class killed MRSA and vancomycin-resistant enterococci, evaded resistance, and reduced bacteria in mouse skin and thigh infections.
milestones.why_it_matters: Shows which chemical parts drive activity, turning a black-box predictor into chemical insight. New antibiotic classes against MRSA are badly needed.

milestones.title: Closed-loop MIT platform designs, makes and tests 294 new dye-like molecules
milestones.summary: MIT's platform linked a generative model, machine-learning property predictors, computer-aided synthesis planning and robotic synthesis and measurement. Across three automatic design-make-test-analyze cycles it made 294 previously unreported dye-like molecules on four human-chosen scaffolds, retraining its models each round; a second study found nine top-performing molecules.
milestones.why_it_matters: Molecular discovery normally cycles slowly through human hands. Automating the whole loop, from idea to measured property, shows how exploration of chemical space could scale.

milestones.title: Satellite AI shows 72-76% of industrial fishing vessels are not publicly tracked
milestones.summary: Deep learning on satellite imagery, matched against vessel GPS data, mapped industrial vessels and offshore infrastructure across the world's coastal waters for 2017-2021. It found 72-76% of industrial fishing vessels and 21-30% of transport and energy vessel activity missing from public tracking, and offshore wind turbines outnumbering oil structures by 2021.

before_after.metric: Industrial fishing vessels not in public tracking systems

milestones.why_it_matters: Oceans feed billions, but untracked fishing escapes oversight. A global map of who is at sea makes enforcement and conservation possible where it was guesswork.
ai_systems: Convolutional neural networks for vessel and infrastructure detection

milestones.title: ML screen of 32 million candidates leads to a sodium-lithium solid electrolyte
milestones.summary: Microsoft and PNNL combined machine-learning models with physics simulations on about 1,000 cloud machines to narrow 32.6 million candidates to about 500,000 likely stable and 18 promising solid electrolytes in under 80 hours. PNNL made and tested the NaxLi3-xYCl6 series; Microsoft says the chosen electrolyte would use about 70% less lithium.

before_after.metric: Candidate materials narrowed to a shortlist
before_after.after: 18 candidates in under 80 hours of cloud computing

milestones.why_it_matters: Lithium is costly and supply-limited. AI-plus-simulation screening shows how teams can move from millions of options to a working prototype in months rather than years.
ai_systems: Machine-learning stability and property models (Azure Quantum Elements)

milestones.title: AlphaGeometry solves olympiad geometry near gold-medallist level
milestones.summary: AlphaGeometry pairs a language model, trained from scratch on millions of synthetic theorems and proofs, with a symbolic deduction engine. On 30 recent olympiad geometry problems it solved 25, against 10 for the previous best method, approaching an average IMO gold medallist and producing human-readable proofs.

before_after.metric: Olympiad geometry problems solved (IMO-AG-30 test)

milestones.why_it_matters: Showed a machine can learn rigorous deduction without human-written proofs by generating its own training data, getting around the scarcity of formal proofs.
milestones.contested_note: Sinha et al. (arXiv:2404.06405, April 2024) showed the reported baseline was weak: Wu's method alone solves 15 problems, and Wu's method plus classic symbolic deduction, with no neural network, solves 21 of the 30.

sources.label: Sinha et al., Wu's method critique, arXiv:2404.06405

milestones.title: RL controller steers DIII-D fusion plasma away from tearing instabilities
milestones.summary: Princeton researchers trained a reinforcement-learning controller on a neural-network model of DIII-D that forecasts tearing instabilities up to 300 ms ahead. In live experiments it adjusted plasma shape and beam power to keep tearing risk below a threshold while holding high-confinement H-mode, even at low safety factor and low torque.

before_after.metric: tearing avoidance at low safety factor and low torque
before_after.after: tearing likelihood held below threshold while keeping H-mode

milestones.why_it_matters: Tearing instabilities are the leading cause of disruptions that end fusion plasmas. Anticipating and steering around them is needed for reactors like ITER to run steadily.

milestones.title: AlphaTensor-Quantum cuts costly T gates in quantum circuits
milestones.summary: Researchers adapted AlphaTensor to minimize T gates, the most expensive operation in fault-tolerant quantum computing. It beat existing T-count optimizers on arithmetic benchmarks, matched the best human-designed circuits for Shor's algorithm and quantum chemistry, and found on its own a Karatsuba-like circuit for finite-field multiplication (a similar human design appeared in 2019).

before_after.metric: Toffoli gates for GF(2^m) multiplication circuits it optimized

milestones.why_it_matters: T gates dominate the cost of running algorithms on future error-corrected quantum computers. Fewer of them means useful quantum computations become possible sooner, on smaller machines.

sources.label: Prior sub-quadratic construction: van Hoof, arXiv, 2019-10-07

milestones.title: AI flood forecasts in ungauged rivers match same-day warnings five days ahead
milestones.summary: Google's AI river model predicts extreme floods in watersheds with no stream gauges as reliably at five days' lead time as the leading global system (GloFAS) does for the same day. It runs in a free public early-warning system covering over 80 countries, expanded in November 2024 to 100 countries and about 700 million people.

before_after.metric: Lead time with GloFAS-nowcast-level reliability in ungauged basins

milestones.why_it_matters: Floods hit hardest where rivers are not measured, mostly in poorer countries. Days of extra warning give families time to move people, animals and belongings.

milestones.title: AI-ECG alerts cut 90-day deaths among hospital patients in randomized trial
milestones.summary: In a multisite randomized trial in Taiwan (15,965 hospitalized patients, 39 physicians), AI-ECG warnings flagging high-risk patients reduced 90-day all-cause mortality from 4.3% to 3.6% (hazard ratio 0.83). Benefit concentrated in high-risk ECGs (HR 0.69), who received more intensive care.

before_after.metric: 90-day all-cause mortality

milestones.why_it_matters: One of the first randomized trials showing an AI alert reduced deaths, not just improved detection; mortality is the outcome that ultimately matters.

milestones.title: AlphaFold 3 predicts joint structures of proteins, DNA, RNA and ligands
milestones.summary: AlphaFold 3 uses a diffusion-based architecture to predict joint structures of complexes containing proteins, nucleic acids, small molecules, ions and modified residues in one model. DeepMind reports about 50% higher accuracy than the best traditional methods on drug-like interactions in the PoseBusters benchmark, with no structural input.
milestones.why_it_matters: Cells run on proteins bound to DNA, RNA and small molecules. One model covering them all lets researchers test binding ideas on screen before going to the lab.
milestones.contested_note: Škrinjar et al. (Nature Structural & Molecular Biology, 2026-05-08) tested leading co-folding methods, AlphaFold 3 among them per the preprint, on 2,600 post-cutoff protein-ligand complexes and concluded they largely memorise ligand poses from training data, limiting use for de novo drug design.

sources.label: Generalization critique, Nature Structural & Molecular Biology, 2026-05-08

milestones.title: ChemCrow agent uses 18 chemistry tools to plan and run syntheses
milestones.summary: EPFL and University of Rochester researchers connected GPT-4 to 18 expert-designed chemistry tools and a robotic synthesis platform. The resulting ChemCrow agent autonomously planned and executed syntheses of an insect repellent and three organocatalysts, and guided the discovery of a new chromophore.
milestones.why_it_matters: Connecting a general language model to specialist software and robots let it complete real chemistry tasks, a pattern now widely used in AI agents for science.

milestones.title: ML-tuned magnetic fields give high fusion performance without edge bursts
milestones.summary: A Princeton-led team used a machine-learning surrogate of a physics code to tune, in real time, the 3D magnetic perturbations applied to the plasma edge on the DIII-D and KSTAR tokamaks. It suppressed damaging edge energy bursts while keeping reactor-relevant core confinement, which the authors report as the highest fusion performance yet without such bursts.

before_after.metric: time to optimize the 3D-field settings
before_after.before: tens of seconds (physics code), so settings were preset before each shot

milestones.why_it_matters: Repeated edge bursts in ITER-class reactors could erode wall components. Suppressing them without losing performance is needed for practical tokamak power plants.
ai_systems: ML-3D (machine-learning surrogate model for real-time 3D-field optimization)

milestones.title: Vision transformer spots small methane leaks in free Sentinel-2 imagery
milestones.summary: A vision transformer overcomes the coarse spectral bands of Sentinel-2 to detect methane point sources down to plumes of 0.01 square kilometres, about 200-300 kg of methane per hour, checked against airborne campaigns. The authors report an order-of-magnitude improvement over the previous state of the art, with global coverage every few days.

before_after.metric: Smallest methane source detectable in Sentinel-2 data
before_after.before: about 10x larger (prior state of the art)

milestones.why_it_matters: Methane causes a large share of current warming, and most comes from a few leaky sites. Spotting them from free satellite data every few days makes fast fixes possible.

milestones.title: One AI planner steers five labs to 21 state-of-the-art organic laser materials
