milestones.summary: Toronto-led teams linked robotic synthesis and in-line measurement at five laboratories around the world, coordinated asynchronously by a cloud-based AI experiment planner, to search for gain materials for organic solid-state lasers. The campaign found 21 new state-of-the-art materials, and gram-scale synthesis confirmed best-in-class stimulated emission in a thin-film device.
milestones.why_it_matters: Expertise and instruments are scattered worldwide. One AI planner coordinating distant labs suggests discovery need not depend on a single well-equipped site.

milestones.title: AgroNT, a language model of 48 plant genomes, scores regulatory DNA
milestones.summary: InstaDeep trained AgroNT, a genome language model, on 48 plant species, mostly crops. It predicts regulatory annotations, promoter and terminator strength and tissue-specific expression, and was used for in-silico saturation mutagenesis of over 10 million cassava mutations, released as a resource.
milestones.why_it_matters: Crop genomes hold many regulatory changes that breeders cannot test one by one. Predicted effects give a ranked starting list, though they still need field and lab checks.

milestones.title: AI-guided polymer dielectrics store 11 times more energy at 200 °C
milestones.summary: Georgia Tech and UConn researchers used AI structure generation and property prediction, with polymer chemistry, to find polynorbornene and polyimide capacitor dielectrics that combine heat stability and high energy density. One stored 8.3 J/cc at 200 °C, eleven times any commercially available polymer dielectric at that temperature.

before_after.metric: Capacitor energy density at 200 °C

milestones.why_it_matters: Electric vehicles, aircraft and grids need capacitors that survive heat. Polymers that keep high energy density at 200 °C fill a gap with no good commercial option.
ai_systems: Machine-learning polymer property predictors and structure generation

milestones.title: NeuralGCM hybrid model matches top weather ensembles and runs decades of climate
milestones.summary: NeuralGCM couples a differentiable atmospheric physics solver with learned components. It is competitive with the best machine-learning models for 1-10-day forecasts and with ECMWF's ensemble for 1-15 days, and tracks climate metrics for decades given sea temperatures, at far lower computing cost. It does not extrapolate to very different future climates.
milestones.why_it_matters: Pure AI forecasters drift over long runs. Keeping physics and learning the hard parts gives a stable, cheap model usable for climate studies, not just next week's weather.

milestones.title: AlphaProof and AlphaGeometry 2 reach IMO silver-medal standard
milestones.summary: On the 2024 International Mathematical Olympiad, DeepMind's systems solved 4 of 6 problems for 28 of 42 points, top of the silver range, graded by Timothy Gowers and Joseph Myers. AlphaProof gave Lean-verified proofs for three, including the hardest problem, but problems were hand-translated into Lean and some took up to three days.

before_after.metric: Best AI score at the IMO

milestones.why_it_matters: First medal-level AI performance at the top pre-university mathematics competition, with machine-checked proofs that cannot hide errors.

milestones.title: The AI Scientist automates machine-learning research from idea to paper
milestones.summary: Sakana AI, Oxford, UBC and Vector Institute researchers built a language-model system that proposes ideas, writes and runs experiment code, plots results, writes a full paper and reviews it with an automated reviewer, for about US$15 per paper. It worked in three machine-learning subfields. An extended version was published in Nature in March 2026.
milestones.why_it_matters: The first public system to run the whole research loop, from idea to written paper, turning the cost and quality of machine-made science into a measurable question.
milestones.contested_note: An independent evaluation (Beel, Kan and Baumgart, SIGIR Forum 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14297) found 42% of experiments failed from coding errors, weak novelty checks, few and outdated citations, and some hallucinated numbers.

milestones.title: Blind study: LLM research ideas rated more novel than experts' ideas
milestones.summary: Stanford researchers had over 100 NLP researchers write research ideas and blind-review both human and LLM-generated ones. AI ideas were judged significantly more novel (p < 0.05) but slightly less feasible. A follow-up in which 43 experts carried out the ideas found the AI ideas' scores fell significantly more than human ideas'.
milestones.why_it_matters: Idea generation is the creative core of research. Testing it blind, then testing whether ideas survive execution, gives a rare controlled measure of AI's research taste.
milestones.contested_note: The authors' own execution study (Si, Hashimoto and Yang, arXiv 2025-06-25, ICLR 2026, https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20803) found LLM ideas' scores dropped significantly more than human ideas after execution, with human ideas scoring higher on many metrics.

milestones.title: Graph foundation model ranks drug repurposing options for 17,080 diseases
milestones.summary: TxGNN, trained on a medical knowledge graph, ranks existing drugs as possible treatments or contraindications for 17,080 diseases, including those with no approved therapy. In stringent zero-shot tests against 8 methods it improved indication accuracy by 49.2% and contraindication accuracy by 35.1%; many predictions matched real off-label prescribing.
milestones.why_it_matters: Most rare diseases have no approved drug. Ranking existing, already-tested drugs for them gives clinicians testable options far faster than developing new ones.
organizations: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai

milestones.title: FlyWire maps all 139,255 neurons and 54.5 million synapses of a fly brain
milestones.summary: A consortium built a wiring diagram of a whole adult fruit-fly brain from electron-microscope images. Neural networks segmented the images and the community proofread them in about 33 person-years. The map has 139,255 neurons and 54.5 million synapses, with cell types and neurotransmitter predictions.

before_after.metric: Neurons in a dense fly brain wiring map

milestones.why_it_matters: Whole-brain wiring lets scientists follow signals from senses to movement across both hemispheres, and it is a template for mapping larger brains.

milestones.title: Big Sleep AI agent finds an exploitable memory bug in SQLite before release
milestones.summary: Google's Big Sleep, a language-model agent from Project Zero and DeepMind, found an exploitable stack buffer underflow in SQLite that existing fuzzing had missed. Developers fixed it the same day, before any official release. Google called it the first public case of an AI agent finding an unknown exploitable memory-safety bug in widely used software.
milestones.why_it_matters: SQLite runs on billions of devices. Finding flaws before attackers do, in code that fuzzers already test heavily, is the core promise of AI for defensive security.

milestones.title: PatternBoost pairs search with transformers to find extremal constructions
milestones.summary: Charton, Ellenberg, Wagner and Williamson alternated a classical local search with a transformer trained on the best constructions found so far, seeding the next round of search. Across several extremal combinatorics problems it found best-known solutions, including a counterexample to a conjecture that had stood for 30 years.
milestones.why_it_matters: Gives mathematicians a general, problem-agnostic tool for finding extreme examples where both intuition and brute-force search fail.

milestones.title: Virtual Lab of AI agents designs nanobodies against new SARS-CoV-2 variants
milestones.summary: Stanford's Virtual Lab had an LLM 'principal investigator' lead LLM scientist agents through research meetings, with light human feedback. The agents built a pipeline combining ESM, AlphaFold-Multimer and Rosetta and designed 92 nanobodies. Lab tests found two with improved binding to the JN.1 or KP.3 variants that still bound the original spike.
milestones.why_it_matters: A team of AI agents planned an interdisciplinary project whose designs worked in the lab, so researchers without a full team of specialists can still do cross-field science.

milestones.title: AlphaQubit neural decoder beats leading decoders on Google quantum hardware
milestones.summary: Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI trained a recurrent transformer to decode surface-code errors. On Sycamore distance-5 experiments (49 qubits) it made 6% fewer errors than tensor-network decoding (2.748% vs 2.915% per round) and 30% fewer than correlated matching, and kept its edge in simulations up to distance 11, though too slow for real-time use.

before_after.metric: logical errors on Sycamore distance-5 data
before_after.after: 30% fewer errors (6% fewer than tensor networks)

milestones.why_it_matters: Quantum computers need constant error correction; better decoding means fewer physical qubits per reliable logical qubit. Learning from real hardware noise beats hand-built noise models.

milestones.title: AI-written fuzz targets find 26 bugs, incl. a likely 20-year-old OpenSSL flaw
milestones.summary: Google used language models to write fuzzing harnesses for OSS-Fuzz projects, extending automated coverage gains to 272 C/C++ projects (from 160) and over 370,000 new lines of code. This found 26 new vulnerabilities, including OpenSSL's low-severity CVE-2024-9143, which Google says was likely present for two decades.

before_after.metric: OSS-Fuzz projects with automated coverage gains

milestones.why_it_matters: Fuzzing only tests code someone wrote a harness for. AI-written harnesses let testing reach neglected code in libraries that secure much of the internet.

milestones.title: AI tool PyTheus suggests a simpler way to entangle photons that never met
milestones.summary: Asked to rediscover entanglement swapping, the design tool PyTheus kept returning a simpler scheme. Nanjing University and Max Planck physicists then demonstrated it, entangling independent photons without direct interaction, prior entanglement or Bell-state measurements, by making the photons' origins indistinguishable (path identity); detecting the partner photons heralds the entanglement.

before_after.metric: requirements to entangle independent photons
before_after.before: prior entangled pairs plus Bell-state measurement

milestones.why_it_matters: Entangling distant particles is the core of quantum networks. A simpler recipe proposed by a machine and confirmed in the lab shows AI can suggest physical concepts, not just tune parameters.
organizations: Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light

milestones.title: GenCast ensemble beats ECMWF's ensemble on 97.2% of targets
milestones.summary: GenCast, a diffusion-based model, generates 15-day global ensemble forecasts at 0.25 degrees for over 80 variables in about 8 minutes. It was more skilful than ECMWF's ENS, the leading operational ensemble, on 97.2% of 1,320 targets (99.8% beyond 36 hours), and better predicted extreme weather, cyclone tracks and wind power.

before_after.metric: Targets where model beats ECMWF ENS

milestones.why_it_matters: Decisions about evacuations or power grids need the odds of each outcome, not one guess. A cheaper, more accurate ensemble gives better probabilities for dangerous weather.

sources.label: Price et al., Nature 637:84, published online 2024-12-04

milestones.title: 41-million-paper study: AI users publish more, but science's focus narrows
milestones.summary: Analysing 41.3 million natural-science papers with a language-model classifier, researchers found scientists doing AI-augmented research publish 3.02 times more papers, receive 4.84 times more citations and lead projects 1.37 years sooner. But AI adoption shrank the range of topics studied by 4.63% and cut scientists' engagement with each other by 22%.
milestones.why_it_matters: It measures AI's real effect on science at scale and flags a risk: AI may pull research toward data-rich, established areas instead of opening new ones.

milestones.title: Closed-loop ML finds hole-transport molecules for 26.2% perovskite solar cells
milestones.summary: Researchers at FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg, KIT and partners paired high-throughput synthesis of organic semiconductors with Bayesian optimization on molecular descriptors. From a small number of model suggestions they found hole-transport materials reaching up to 26.2% power conversion efficiency (25.9% certified) in perovskite solar cells.
milestones.why_it_matters: Solar-cell efficiency depends on many specialized layer materials. Learning from small, self-generated datasets lets niche fields design molecules without large existing databases.

milestones.title: Deep learning designs millimetre-wave chip structures in minutes, not weeks
milestones.summary: Princeton and IIT Madras engineers trained deep networks to predict the electromagnetic behaviour of arbitrary pixelated shapes, then searched for shapes meeting a target. Irregular designs built in a 90-nm chip process included an amplifier with about 17.5 dB peak gain from 23.6 to 37.3 GHz. Once trained, each design took minutes.

before_after.metric: Design time for mm-wave passive structures

milestones.why_it_matters: Wireless and sensing chips are limited by the shapes human designers know; letting AI explore unfamiliar geometries opens designs outside the standard templates.
ai_systems: CNN electromagnetic emulator with inverse-design search

milestones.title: Real-world AI use in German breast screening raises cancer detection 17.6%
milestones.summary: In Germany's PRAIM observational implementation study (463,094 women, 119 radiologists, 12 sites), radiologists using AI-supported double reading detected 6.7 cancers per 1,000 versus 5.7 without, a 17.6% increase, while recall rates did not rise (37.4 vs 38.3 per 1,000). Radiologists chose case-by-case whether to use AI.

before_after.metric: Cancers detected per 1,000 screened

milestones.why_it_matters: Shows trial-level benefits can hold up in routine national screening, where much promising medical AI has historically faltered.

milestones.title: AI-designed proteins neutralize deadly snake venom toxins in mice
milestones.summary: Using deep-learning protein design, the Baker lab and partners created new proteins that bind three-finger toxins from elapid snake venoms. With limited lab screening, designs bound tightly, matched computational models at near-atomic accuracy, neutralized all three toxin subfamilies in vitro, and protected mice from lethal neurotoxin challenge.
milestones.why_it_matters: Snakebite kills over 100,000 people a year, mostly in poor rural areas. Stable, cheap-to-make designed proteins could replace costly antibodies from immunized animals.
organizations: Institute for Protein Design, University of Washington

milestones.title: ESM3 generates a fluorescent protein only 58% identical to known ones
milestones.summary: EvolutionaryScale's ESM3, a generative model reasoning over protein sequence, structure and function, was prompted to design fluorescent proteins. Of those synthesized, one bright protein, esmGFP, shares 58% sequence identity with known fluorescent proteins, which the authors estimate equals about 500 million years of evolution.
milestones.why_it_matters: Shows a language model can propose functional proteins far from anything known, widening the search space for enzymes, sensors and therapeutics beyond what evolution sampled.

milestones.title: MatterGen generates candidate crystals to order; one design is synthesized
milestones.summary: Microsoft Research's MatterGen, a diffusion model, generates inorganic crystals steerable toward target chemistry, symmetry and properties; its outputs were over twice as likely to be new and stable as earlier generative models'. One design, TaCr2O6, was made as a disordered phase with bulk modulus estimated at up to 169 GPa against a 200 GPa target.

before_after.metric: Share of generated structures that are new and stable

milestones.why_it_matters: Instead of screening known lists, generative models propose materials that meet a specification directly, which could shorten design of batteries, magnets and catalysts if outputs are truly new.
milestones.contested_note: Juelsholt (ChemRxiv 2025-06-19; Materials Horizons 2026) showed the synthesized disordered phase matches Ta1/2Cr1/2O2, a compound reported in 1972 and present in MatterGen's training data, so the showcased compound was not new.

milestones.title: ML-designed carbon nanolattices reach steel's strength at foam's density
milestones.summary: Researchers at Toronto, KAIST and partners used multi-objective Bayesian optimization to reshape nanoscale lattice struts, then 3D-printed them by two-photon polymerization and converted them to carbon. Optimized lattices were up to 118% stronger and 68% stiffer than standard designs at equal density, matching carbon steel's strength at Styrofoam's density.

before_after.metric: Strength and stiffness at equal density vs standard lattice

milestones.why_it_matters: Lighter parts with the same strength cut fuel use in aircraft and vehicles; machine-guided design found geometries that spread stress better than standard shapes.

milestones.title: ExoMiner++ vets 147,568 TESS signals and flags 7,330 planet candidates
milestones.summary: NASA's ExoMiner++ adds periodograms, difference images and spacecraft data, and trains on Kepler and TESS labels together. Of 147,568 unlabelled TESS 2-minute signals it classified 7,330 as planet candidates, including 50 new community candidates, and kept 1,797 of 2,506 existing TESS candidates as likely planets. These are candidates, not confirmed planets.

before_after.metric: ExoFOP TESS planet candidates (TOIs) ExoMiner++ still rates as candidates

milestones.why_it_matters: Follow-up telescope time is scarce. Ranking candidates by how likely they are to be real lets observers confirm more planets for the same effort.

sources.label: Valizadegan et al., The Astronomical Journal 170:287, 2025-10-28

milestones.title: Deep-learning design creates working serine hydrolase enzymes from scratch
milestones.summary: University of Washington researchers used the generative model RFdiffusion plus PLACER, a neural network that checks active-site geometry at each reaction step, to design serine hydrolases from minimal active-site descriptions. Designs were catalytically active, crystal structures matched models within 1 Å, and working enzymes came in five folds never seen in natural serine hydrolases.
milestones.why_it_matters: Enzymes that run multistep reactions could make chemical manufacturing cleaner. Designing them from scratch, rather than tweaking natural ones, opens catalysts for reactions nature never evolved.
organizations: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design

milestones.title: LLM prescreening nearly doubles clinical-trial enrollment in randomized test
milestones.summary: At Mass General Brigham, 4,476 patients were randomized to manual or LLM-assisted (RECTIFIER) eligibility prescreening for a heart-failure trial. AI assistance reached decisions faster (hazard ratio 1.78), identified more eligible patients (20.4% vs 12.7%) and enrolled 35 versus 19 patients.

before_after.metric: Patients enrolled

milestones.why_it_matters: Slow recruitment delays or sinks many clinical trials. Faster, accurate chart screening shortens the time to answers about new treatments.

milestones.title: AI co-scientist's top hypothesis matches an unpublished, lab-confirmed mechanism
milestones.summary: Google's Gemini-based multi-agent co-scientist generates, debates and ranks hypotheses. Asked how cf-PICI genetic islands spread across bacterial species, its top-ranked hypothesis matched a mechanism Imperial College researchers had confirmed but not published: hijacking diverse phage tails. Expert-selected leukaemia drug candidates it proposed also inhibited cancer cells in vitro.
milestones.why_it_matters: Matching a hidden, lab-confirmed answer is a clean test of hypothesis generation, the slow creative step of science, and suggests AI can shorten it.

milestones.title: ECMWF runs its machine-learning forecast model operationally
milestones.summary: ECMWF made its machine-learning model AIFS Single operational on 25 February 2025, alongside the physics-based IFS, followed by the 51-member AIFS ensemble on 1 July 2025. ECMWF reports gains of up to 20% on measures such as cyclone tracks and surface temperature, using about 1,000 times less energy, on a coarser 28-31 km grid.

before_after.metric: Energy per forecast vs physics-based IFS

milestones.why_it_matters: ECMWF sets the global standard for forecasting. Its adoption moved AI weather models from research papers into the forecasts that national services rely on every day.

milestones.title: Machine learning analyses neutron-star merger signals in one second
milestones.summary: A neural posterior estimation framework performs complete parameter inference for binary neutron star mergers in about one second without the usual approximations. It can localize sources before merger, improves sky localization by about 30% over approximate low-latency methods, and scales to hour-long signals expected from next-generation detectors.

before_after.metric: Sky-localization precision vs approximate low-latency methods

milestones.why_it_matters: Telescopes must point at a merger within minutes to catch its light. Fast, accurate locations from the gravitational-wave signal make those joint observations far more likely.
organizations: Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems
Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics

milestones.title: Fully AI-generated paper clears first-round review at an ICLR 2025 workshop
milestones.summary: Sakana's AI Scientist-v2 wrote papers with no human edits; researchers filtered its outputs and submitted three, with the organisers' consent, to an ICLR 2025 workshop that accepted about 70% of papers. One scored 6, 7 and 6 (average 6.33), above the acceptance threshold. It was withdrawn before final decision, as agreed.

before_after.metric: Peer-review scores of a fully AI-generated paper
before_after.before: No fully AI-written paper had passed peer review

milestones.why_it_matters: Peer review is science's quality gate. A machine-written paper getting through, even at a lenient workshop, shows that gate now faces AI-made work and must adapt.
milestones.contested_note: Researchers quoted by TechCrunch (2025-03-12, https://techcrunch.com/2025/03/12/sakana-claims-its-ai-paper-passed-peer-review-but-its-a-bit-more-nuanced-than-that/) called the result misleading: humans picked which papers to submit, the workshop was lenient and the paper skipped meta-review. Sakana also found citation errors in it.

milestones.title: Euclid's first data: AI-led search finds about 500 strong lens candidates
milestones.summary: Five machine-learning models, led by a fine-tuned Zoobot network, ranked about one million objects in Euclid's 63-square-degree quick release; citizen scientists and experts then inspected the top candidates. The result was 250 grade A and 247 grade B galaxy-scale lenses, almost all previously unknown. Extrapolated to the full survey, about 75,000 are expected.

before_after.metric: Galaxy-scale strong lenses found in Euclid Q1 (grade A + B)

milestones.why_it_matters: Strong lenses act as natural magnifying glasses that weigh dark matter and measure cosmic expansion. Machine ranking makes finding tens of thousands of them feasible.

sources.label: Euclid Collaboration: Lines et al., Astronomy & Astrophysics 711:A28, 2026

milestones.title: Aardvark Weather goes from raw observations to forecasts with one AI model
milestones.summary: Aardvark Weather takes raw observations and directly produces global and local station forecasts, with no numerical model at run time. On a coarse 1.5-degree grid it matched or beat the US GFS on most headline variables but not ECMWF's HRES. Station forecasts stayed skilful to ten days, competitive with bias-corrected HRES.

before_after.metric: Parts of the forecast pipeline done by machine learning
before_after.after: observations to local forecasts, end to end

milestones.why_it_matters: Conventional forecasting needs supercomputers and large teams. A single learned system could let countries with little computing produce and tailor their own forecasts.

milestones.title: Conversational AI outperforms primary-care doctors in simulated consultations
milestones.summary: In a randomized, double-blind crossover study of text consultations with patient-actors (159 scenarios, 20 primary-care physicians; Canada, UK, India), Google's AMIE had higher diagnostic accuracy and was rated better on 30 of 32 axes by specialists and 25 of 26 by patient-actors. Text chat is unfamiliar to doctors; no real patients.
milestones.why_it_matters: History-taking is the core of diagnosis. If AI can do it well and safely, expert-level first consultations could reach places with few doctors.

milestones.title: MICrONS joins activity and wiring in a cubic millimetre of mouse cortex
milestones.summary: MICrONS recorded calcium activity of about 75,000 neurons in an awake mouse's visual cortex, then reconstructed the same cubic millimetre from electron microscopy: over 200,000 cells and about 0.5 billion synapses. Convolutional networks did the automated tracing; a subset of neurons was proofread by hand. The data are open.
milestones.why_it_matters: Linking what neurons do to how they are wired lets scientists test circuit rules directly, across thousands of neurons in one animal.

sources.label: MICrONS Explorer, cortical mm3 dataset page

milestones.title: Urania algorithm designs gravitational-wave detectors beating human designs
milestones.summary: Max Planck and Caltech researchers recast interferometer design as a continuous optimization problem solved with methods inspired by machine learning. The algorithm Urania found about 50 detector layouts that outperform the best known next-generation designs under realistic constraints, raising the potentially observable volume of the Universe by up to 50-fold. None has been built yet.

before_after.metric: potentially observable volume of the Universe

milestones.why_it_matters: Detector sensitivity limits which cosmic events we can observe. Automated design explores layouts humans never considered and can reveal new physics ideas behind better instruments.
organizations: Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light

sources.label: Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light, 2025-04-14

milestones.title: Peer-reviewed study: driverless Waymo cars had far fewer injury crashes
milestones.summary: Waymo-authored research compared 56.7 million driverless miles with matched human benchmarks. Rates were significantly lower for injury, airbag-deployment and serious-injury crashes, with no crash type significantly worse; Waymo reports 85% fewer serious-injury and 92% fewer pedestrian-injury crashes. Company data to June 2026 (271 million miles) show 82% fewer injury crashes.

before_after.metric: Crashes with suspected serious or worse injury, vs human benchmark

milestones.why_it_matters: Road crashes are a leading cause of death. Large-scale evidence that a learned driving system is safer than people is a milestone for trusting AI with life-critical physical tasks.

milestones.title: AI co-scientist proposes liver-fibrosis drug candidates confirmed in organoids
milestones.summary: Google's multi-agent AI co-scientist proposed repurposing drugs that target epigenetic regulators for liver fibrosis. Stanford researchers tested them in human liver organoids: two of three AI-recommended drugs showed significant anti-fibrotic activity, and vorinostat, an approved cancer drug, cut TGF-beta-induced chromatin changes by 91% and promoted regeneration.
milestones.why_it_matters: An AI generating treatment hypotheses that survive lab tests suggests machines can speed the slow, guess-heavy front end of drug repurposing.

milestones.title: AlphaEvolve evolves code that saves compute across Google's infrastructure
milestones.summary: AlphaEvolve, a Gemini-powered agent that evolves code against automatic evaluators, produced a data-center scheduling heuristic that recovers about 0.7% of Google's worldwide compute, a 23% faster kernel that cut Gemini training time 1%, up to 32.5% faster FlashAttention kernels, and a simplified circuit adopted in an upcoming TPU.

before_after.metric: Google fleet compute recovered by scheduling

milestones.why_it_matters: At Google's scale, fractions of a percent equal whole data centres. A general agent improving real production code shows AI can now speed up the very systems that build AI.

milestones.title: AlphaEvolve improves best-known results on about 20% of 50+ open problems
milestones.summary: Google DeepMind's Gemini-powered evolutionary coding agent was run on over 50 open problems in analysis, geometry and combinatorics: it rediscovered the state of the art in about 75% and improved it in about 20%. It found a 48-multiplication method for 4×4 complex matrices and raised the 11-dimensional kissing number bound to 593.

before_after.metric: Scalar multiplications for 4×4 complex matrices

milestones.why_it_matters: A general-purpose LLM agent with automatic checking pushed many separate mathematical records at once, rather than one hand-picked problem.

milestones.title: Multi-agent AI Robin proposes ripasudil as a dry macular degeneration candidate
milestones.summary: FutureHouse's Robin generated hypotheses, proposed experiments and analyzed data while humans ran the lab work. It proposed boosting retinal-pigment-cell phagocytosis and identified ripasudil, a glaucoma drug not previously proposed for dry AMD, which raised phagocytosis in vitro (1.89-fold by Robin's analysis; 1.75-fold by human analysis). Published in Nature, May 2026.
milestones.why_it_matters: Points to AI systems running most of the reasoning loop of discovery. The candidate is still a cell-culture result with no patient data.

milestones.title: Aurora model beats operational forecasts for air quality, waves and cyclones
milestones.summary: Microsoft's Aurora, pretrained on more than one million hours of varied geophysical data and then fine-tuned, outperformed operational forecasts for air quality, ocean waves, tropical cyclone tracks and high-resolution weather, at orders of magnitude lower computing cost.
milestones.why_it_matters: One pretrained model adapted cheaply to many Earth problems means accurate forecasts of smog, swell or storms no longer each need a separate expensive system.

milestones.title: OpenAI o3 finds a remote use-after-free bug in the Linux kernel's SMB server
milestones.summary: Security researcher Sean Heelan gave OpenAI's o3 about 12,000 lines of the Linux kernel's ksmbd code through the plain API, with no tools or agent scaffolding. It identified a previously unknown use-after-free in the session logoff handler, now CVE-2025-37899. Output was noisy: Heelan estimated a signal-to-noise ratio of about 1:50.
milestones.why_it_matters: A general model, prompted plainly, found a subtle concurrency bug the expert running it had not spotted. It showed AI code auditing is within reach of individual researchers, not only large labs.

milestones.title: AI-discovered lung-fibrosis drug shows safety and early signal in phase 2a
milestones.summary: Rentosertib, a TNIK inhibitor whose target and molecule came from generative AI, was given to 71 IPF patients for 12 weeks. Adverse-event rates resembled placebo (primary endpoint). Lung capacity (FVC, secondary endpoint) rose 98.4 mL on 60 mg daily versus a 20.3 mL fall on placebo. A 320-patient phase 3 started September 2026.

before_after.metric: 12-week change in FVC (secondary endpoint)

milestones.why_it_matters: Reported as the first randomized patient data for a drug whose target and molecule both came from generative AI. Small and short, so efficacy remains unproven until phase 3.

milestones.title: Robot autonomously performs gallbladder-removal steps on 8 of 8 organs
milestones.summary: SRT-H, from Johns Hopkins and Stanford, learned from demonstrations: a high-level policy plans in language and issues corrective instructions, and a low-level policy moves the instruments. It performed long sequences of cholecystectomy steps on eight ex vivo pig gallbladders with 100% success and no human intervention.

before_after.metric: Fully autonomous success on ex vivo cholecystectomy steps
before_after.before: Autonomy limited to simple tasks in controlled settings

milestones.why_it_matters: Tissue varies from patient to patient. A robot that plans, notices its errors and recovers on real tissue is a step toward consistent surgery where skilled surgeons are scarce.

milestones.title: OpenAI experimental model scores at gold-medal level on IMO 2025
milestones.summary: An experimental OpenAI reasoning model solved 5 of 6 IMO 2025 problems for 35 of 42 points under exam conditions: two 4.5-hour sessions, no tools or internet, natural-language proofs. Three former IMO medalists graded the proofs by consensus; the IMO did not officially grade the entry. The proofs were published on GitHub.

before_after.metric: Best AI score at the IMO

milestones.why_it_matters: A general-purpose language model, not a maths-specific system, wrote olympiad proofs at gold level within human time limits, a capability step directly relevant to research.

milestones.title: Gemini Deep Think certified at IMO gold-medal standard
milestones.summary: An advanced version of Google's Gemini Deep Think solved 5 of 6 IMO 2025 problems for 35 of 42 points, within the 4.5-hour limit, writing natural-language proofs from the official problem statements. IMO coordinators graded and certified the answers by student criteria; they did not validate the system itself.

before_after.metric: Best officially graded AI score at the IMO

milestones.why_it_matters: First gold-level AI result checked by the competition's own graders, showing natural-language reasoning had overtaken specialist formal systems within a year.

milestones.title: LLM safety net cut diagnostic errors 16% in Kenyan primary-care clinics
milestones.summary: Penda Health and OpenAI studied 39,849 visits across 15 Nairobi primary-care clinics, randomly giving half the clinicians AI Consult, a GPT-4o tool that flags possible errors. Those clinicians made 16% fewer diagnostic and 13% fewer treatment errors, as rated by independent physicians. Patient outcomes were not the endpoint.
milestones.why_it_matters: Clinics in low-income settings face heavy patient loads with few specialists. A well-integrated safety net could raise care quality cheaply, but patient-outcome benefit is not yet shown.
milestones.contested_note: A 2026 cluster-randomized trial in 16 Kenyan primary-care facilities (Nature Medicine; 9,691 patients; KEMRI-Wellcome, PATH, Penda) found LLM assistance safe but no significant cut in 14-day treatment failure (2.2% vs 2.0%; aOR 0.77, P=0.13). A 2026 retrospective safety evaluation (Nature Health) found actively harmful AI suggestions in 7.8% of encounters.

milestones.title: AI-designed OpenCRISPR-1 edits human cells, about 400 mutations from SpCas9
milestones.summary: Profluent mined over 1 million CRISPR operons from 26 terabases of sequence and trained language models that generated 4.8 times as many protein clusters across CRISPR-Cas families as nature holds. Several designed editors matched or beat SpCas9 in activity and specificity despite about 400 mutations; OpenCRISPR-1 also works with base editing.
milestones.why_it_matters: Natural editors come from microbes and often work poorly in human cells. Designing editors with AI can bypass evolutionary constraints and widen the gene-editing toolbox.

milestones.title: Physics-tailored machine learning uncovers unexpected forces in dusty plasma
milestones.summary: Emory physicists trained a neural network with built-in physical symmetries on 3D particle trajectories from a laboratory dusty plasma. It learned the non-reciprocal forces between particles with R² above 0.99, and enabled measurements of particle charge and screening length that deviate strongly from common theoretical assumptions.
milestones.why_it_matters: Dusty plasmas are common in space and around planets. Learning force laws directly from particle motion, in an interpretable way, can correct theory for many-particle systems.

milestones.title: DARPA AI Cyber Challenge: autonomous systems find and patch open-source bugs
milestones.summary: At the final of DARPA's two-year AI Cyber Challenge at DEF CON 33, autonomous systems combining language models and program analysis found 54 of 63 planted vulnerabilities and patched 43. They also found 18 real, unplanted vulnerabilities, averaging 45 minutes per patch and about $152 per task. Team Atlanta won; the systems are being open-sourced.

before_after.metric: Planted vulnerabilities in the final round

milestones.why_it_matters: Open-source code underpins hospitals, power grids and banks, and its maintainers are stretched thin. Cheap automatic finding and fixing of bugs could close holes before attackers use them.
organizations: Team Atlanta (Georgia Tech, Samsung Research, KAIST, POSTECH)

milestones.title: Generative AI designs new antibiotics active against gonorrhoea and MRSA
milestones.summary: MIT and Broad researchers used fragment-based and unconstrained generative models (genetic algorithms, variational autoencoders) to design novel molecules against Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Staphylococcus aureus. Of 24 synthesized compounds, 7 showed selective antibacterial activity; two leads with distinct mechanisms reduced bacterial burden in mouse gonorrhoea and MRSA skin infections.
milestones.why_it_matters: Moves AI from searching existing chemical libraries to inventing molecules never made before, reaching chemical space that libraries do not cover.

milestones.title: Deep-learning model forecast NIF's first fusion ignition as the likely outcome
milestones.summary: Before the December 2022 shot that first achieved fusion ignition, LLNL's generative model combining simulations, deep learning, experimental data and Bayesian statistics, trained on over 150,000 simulations, gave ignition a probability above 70% (74% per LLNL), far higher than for earlier designs. The measured yield fell within the predicted range.

before_after.metric: forecast ignition probability for the shot design
before_after.after: 74% for the December 2022 design, which ignited

milestones.why_it_matters: Laser fusion shots are rare and costly. Calibrated AI forecasts let scientists judge designs before firing and quantify uncertainty, speeding the path toward fusion energy.
ai_systems: LLNL CogSim physics-informed deep learning model

milestones.title: Gauss agent completes Lean formalization of the strong Prime Number Theorem
milestones.summary: Math Inc.'s autoformalization agent Gauss finished, in three weeks, the strong Prime Number Theorem formalization challenge that Terence Tao and Alex Kontorovich set in January 2024, producing about 25,000 lines of Lean and over 1,000 theorems and definitions, including missing complex-analysis results. Human experts supplied natural-language scaffolding.

before_after.metric: Strong PNT in Lean
before_after.before: Incomplete after ~18 months of human effort

milestones.why_it_matters: Machine-checked proofs remove doubt about correctness but were slow to write; cutting months to weeks makes verifying serious mathematics practical.

milestones.title: Deep Loop Shaping cuts LIGO mirror control noise by 30 to 100 times
milestones.summary: Google DeepMind, Caltech and the Gran Sasso Science Institute used reinforcement learning with frequency-domain rewards to design a controller for one of LIGO's hardest mirror-stabilization loops. Tested at LIGO Livingston, it cut control noise in the 10–30 Hz band by over 30 times, and up to 100 times in sub-bands, beating the quantum-limit design goal.

before_after.metric: control noise, 10–30 Hz band

milestones.why_it_matters: Control noise blinds detectors at low frequencies, where heavier black-hole mergers and early neutron-star warnings appear. Quieter control could let LIGO detect more events.

milestones.title: Google's ERA writes scientific software that beats expert leaderboards
milestones.summary: Google's ERA pairs a language model with tree search to write code that maximises a score, often building on published methods. It produced 40 single-cell data-integration methods that beat the top human methods on a public leaderboard (best 14% above ComBat) and, in a retrospective test, 14 COVID-19 forecasters that beat the CDC ensemble.

before_after.metric: Single-cell batch-integration score (OpenProblems leaderboard)
before_after.after: About 14% higher; 40 AI methods beat top human methods

milestones.why_it_matters: Much research waits on slow, specialised software. A system that searches the space of programs against a measurable goal can speed many empirical sciences at once.

milestones.title: LLM agents evolve SAT solvers that beat 2025 winners in the authors' tests
milestones.summary: NVIDIA researchers used Claude-based coding agents in Cursor to evolve entire SAT-solver codebases, tens of thousands of lines of C/C++, under correctness checks and benchmark feedback, with human steering in later stages. Starting only from 2024 competition solvers and instances, the evolved solvers beat the 2025 winners' PAR-2 scores in the authors' own reruns.

before_after.metric: PAR-2 score on SAT Competition 2025 benchmark (authors' reruns)

milestones.why_it_matters: SAT solvers check chip designs, software and schedules. AI agents improving a mature, heavily tuned codebase as a whole, not just small kernels, widens what automated discovery can reach.

milestones.title: GPT-style model forecasts risk of over 1,000 diseases from health records
milestones.summary: Delphi-2M, a modified GPT model trained on 400,000 UK Biobank participants and validated without changes on 1.9 million Danish records, predicts rates of more than 1,000 diseases from a person's medical history, with accuracy comparable to single-disease models, and can simulate health trajectories up to 20 years ahead.
milestones.why_it_matters: Health systems usually plan prevention one disease at a time. One model of how diseases follow each other could target screening to those most at risk.

milestones.title: AI systems reach gold-medal level at ICPC World Finals; one solves all 12
milestones.summary: At the 2025 ICPC World Finals, working under contest rules with official judging, OpenAI's system (GPT-5 plus an experimental reasoning model) solved all 12 problems; the best of 139 human teams solved 11. Google's Gemini 2.5 Deep Think solved 10, including one no university team solved, which would have ranked second.

before_after.metric: Problems solved, ICPC World Finals 2025

milestones.why_it_matters: Contest problems are new algorithmic puzzles solved under time pressure. Beating the best student teams shows AI can reliably design and implement correct algorithms, a core research skill.

milestones.title: Neural-network solvers discover unstable singularities in fluid equations
milestones.summary: Google DeepMind with mathematicians from Brown, NYU and Stanford combined purpose-built neural networks with a high-precision Gauss–Newton optimizer to find the first systematic families of unstable self-similar blow-up solutions, for the incompressible porous media and 3D Euler (with boundary) equations, some near double-float machine precision.
milestones.why_it_matters: Unstable singularities are thought central to whether Euler or Navier–Stokes flows can blow up, a Millennium Prize question; precise candidates are a route to computer-assisted proofs.

milestones.title: MIT's CRESt platform finds eight-element fuel-cell catalyst in three months
milestones.summary: MIT's CRESt joined multimodal models that read compositions, literature text and microscope images with knowledge-assisted Bayesian optimization, robotics and camera monitoring. In three months it explored over 900 catalyst chemistries and ran 3,500 electrochemical tests, finding a Pd-Pt-Cu-Au-Ir-Ce-Nb-Cr formate-oxidation catalyst with 9.3-fold better cost-specific performance.

before_after.metric: Cost-specific performance, formate oxidation catalyst

milestones.why_it_matters: Fuel cells depend on scarce precious metals. Systems that read papers, watch experiments and diagnose their own errors can search element mixtures too vast for people.
ai_systems: CRESt (large multimodal models with knowledge-assisted Bayesian optimization)

milestones.title: GPT-5 suggests a key proof step in a quantum complexity paper
milestones.summary: Scott Aaronson and Freek Witteveen proved that black-box amplification in the quantum class QMA cannot push completeness closer to 1 than doubly exponential. In the first version the key function in the proof was suggested by GPT-5 Thinking; the published version (Quantum, October 2026) uses a simpler function proposed by new coauthor Phillip Harris.
milestones.why_it_matters: A leading theorist publicly credited an AI with a key technical step in a research proof, an early sign of AI as a working research assistant.

milestones.title: GPT-5 'solves' 10 Erdős problems, but had found existing solutions
milestones.summary: OpenAI's Kevin Weil posted that GPT-5 'found solutions to 10 (!) previously unsolved Erdős problems' and progressed on 11 others. Site maintainer Thomas Bloom called it 'a dramatic misrepresentation': GPT-5 had located published papers he did not know about. The post was deleted, though the searches did update the database.

before_after.metric: New solutions to open Erdős problems

milestones.why_it_matters: Showed AI literature search can surface forgotten results, and that claims of AI discovery must be checked against prior work before being announced.
milestones.contested_note: Thomas Bloom (erdosproblems.com) called the claim 'a dramatic misrepresentation'; Demis Hassabis wrote 'This is embarrassing'; Sébastien Bubeck conceded only literature solutions were found (TechCrunch, 2025-10-19).

milestones.title: CodeMender agent upstreams 72 security fixes to open-source projects
milestones.summary: Google DeepMind's CodeMender, built on Gemini Deep Think with fuzzing, static analysis and differential testing, writes and self-checks security patches. In six months of development it upstreamed 72 security fixes to open-source projects, some as large as 4.5 million lines of code; human researchers reviewed every patch before submission.
milestones.why_it_matters: Finding bugs is only half the job; someone must fix them correctly. Agents that write sound patches could let fixing keep pace as AI speeds up bug discovery.

milestones.title: 27-billion-parameter cell model proposes a drug that held up in lab cells
milestones.summary: Google and Yale trained a 27-billion-parameter language model on single-cell data. A virtual screen nominated silmitasertib, a CK2 inhibitor, to raise antigen presentation only in an immune-active context. In human cell models unseen in training, silmitasertib plus low-dose interferon raised it roughly 50%, per the developers. Cell tests only; preprint.
milestones.why_it_matters: Antigen presentation is a key immune trigger. A model that proposes a context-specific drug effect that then holds in cells is an early case of AI-guided hypothesis generation in biology.

sources.label: bioRxiv preprint, posted 2025-04-17, revised 2025-10-11 and later

milestones.title: Machine-discovered reinforcement learning rule beats human-designed ones
milestones.summary: DeepMind meta-learned a reinforcement learning update rule from the experience of a population of agents across many environments. The discovered rule, Disco57, scored an interquartile mean of 13.86 on the 57-game Atari benchmark, beating all existing hand-designed rules including MuZero, and reached state of the art on unseen benchmarks such as ProcGen.

before_after.metric: Atari-57 human-normalized IQM score

milestones.why_it_matters: Learning algorithms have been designed by hand for decades. Machines discovering better ones suggests future AI methods may be found automatically from experience.

milestones.title: Fully automated AI lifestyle coach matches human coaches for prediabetes
milestones.summary: In a 368-person randomized noninferiority trial at two US sites led by Johns Hopkins, referral to a fully automated, app-based AI Diabetes Prevention Program met the composite weight, activity and HbA1c goal as often as human-coached programs (31.7% vs 31.9%). More people started the AI program (93.4% vs 82.7%).

before_after.metric: Participants reaching composite prevention goal at 12 months

milestones.why_it_matters: Proven diabetes-prevention coaching is underused because human coaches are scarce. An automated coach that works as well could scale prevention cheaply.

milestones.title: AlphaEvolve tested on 67 problems with Tao and Gómez-Serrano
milestones.summary: Bogdan Georgiev, Javier Gómez-Serrano, Terence Tao and Adam Zsolt Wagner ran AlphaEvolve on 67 problems. It rediscovered the best known constructions in most cases, improved several, sometimes generalized finite results into formulas valid for all inputs, and was combined with Deep Think and AlphaProof to generate proofs.
milestones.why_it_matters: A systematic test by leading mathematicians across dozens of problems, mapping where AI search helps and where it does not, instead of one cherry-picked success.

milestones.title: Kosmos AI scientist runs 12-hour autonomous data-driven research campaigns
milestones.summary: Kosmos runs up to 12 hours, reading about 1,500 papers and executing 42,000 lines of code per run, coordinated through a structured world model. Independent scientists judged 79.4% of its report statements accurate; collaborators said a run equalled about six months of their work. Three of seven highlighted discoveries matched findings it had not seen.
milestones.why_it_matters: Staying coherent over hundreds of steps lets an AI pursue a question in depth, so data-rich fields could test far more hypotheses than human teams have time for.

milestones.title: Reinforcement learning sets new kissing-number records in dimensions 25 to 31
milestones.summary: PackingStar, a reinforcement learning system that treats the kissing number problem as a two-player game of filling in tables of cosines between sphere centres, beat the best known lower bounds in every dimension from 25 to 31, for example from 197,048 to 197,056 touching spheres in 25 dimensions and from 232,874 to 238,350 in 31.

before_after.metric: Kissing number lower bound in 31 dimensions

milestones.why_it_matters: The kissing number, how many equal spheres can touch a central one, is known exactly in only six dimensions; the old records in dimensions 25 to 31 all came from one Leech-lattice construction.
organizations: Shanghai Academy of AI for Science
milestones.contested_note: The configurations are explicit and checkable but not yet peer-reviewed. The 13-dimensional 1,146 beats only the 1,130 rational construction of 1971, not the 1,154 record. The September 2026 revision reports 15 improved bounds across kissing-type problems.

sources.label: Ma et al., Finding Kissing Numbers with Game-theoretic Reinforcement Learning, arXiv:2511.13391

milestones.title: GPT-5 case studies include four new maths results, among them Erdős #848
milestones.summary: OpenAI and academic collaborators documented GPT-5 in live research, including four new, human-verified mathematics results. In one, GPT-5 Pro supplied an idea that, with earlier online comments, let Mehtaab Sawhney settle Erdős problem #848: for large N, the numbers ≡ 7 (mod 25) form a largest set in which no product-plus-one ab+1 is squarefree.
milestones.why_it_matters: It records, with transcripts, where a general-purpose model actually moved research forward and where it failed, giving mathematicians concrete evidence rather than anecdotes.
milestones.contested_note: The authors call the new results modest in scope. For #848, GPT-5's own attempts at a full proof had numerous errors; Sawhney turned its idea into the proof.

sources.label: Bubeck et al., Early science acceleration experiments with GPT-5, arXiv:2511.16072
OpenAI, Early experiments in accelerating science with GPT-5 (2025-11-20)

milestones.title: Aristotle proves a version of Erdős problem #124 in Lean on its own
milestones.summary: Working only from a formal statement in the Formal Conjectures project, Harmonic's Aristotle spent six hours on a Lean proof that, whenever 1/(d₁−1)+…+1/(d_r−1) ≥ 1, every whole number is a sum of one number per base dᵢ with base-dᵢ digits all 0 or 1. Boris Alexeev posted it on 29 November 2025.
milestones.why_it_matters: An early case of an AI prover settling a listed problem end to end, and a lesson in how loosely stated problems can make 'solved' claims misleading.
milestones.contested_note: Thomas Bloom (forum, 30 Nov 2025): Aristotle solved 'a' version, with an olympiad-style proof, but not 'the' version; the Burr–Erdős–Graham–Li form, which excludes the digit 1s, remains open. The original formal statement also had a typo that weakened it, which Alexeev corrected.

milestones.title: AxiomProver writes Lean proofs for all 12 Putnam 2025 problems
milestones.summary: Axiom's AxiomProver received the Putnam 2025 problems section by section from an official proctor on 6 December 2025 and autonomously produced Lean proofs for all 12, eight of them before the exam closed. Axiom released the machine-checked proofs with commentary on 8 January 2026.
milestones.why_it_matters: Every answer is machine-checked, so no human grader is needed to trust it. A formal prover handled a full, unseen, hard exam under time pressure.
milestones.contested_note: Timing (8 of 12 within the exam window) is Axiom's own account, and a technical report was still to come. Some proofs are long and brute-force, such as a 1,061-line case analysis for B4.

sources.label: Axiom, From Seeing Why to Checking Everything (2026-01-08)

milestones.title: AlphaQubit 2 decodes surface and colour quantum codes in real time
milestones.summary: Google's AlphaQubit 2 neural decoder reached near-optimal logical error rates for surface and colour codes in realistic-noise simulations and matched AlphaQubit 1 on Willow chip data. It decoded in under 1 µs per cycle on commercial accelerators: the surface code up to distance 11 and, a first, the colour code up to distance 9.

before_after.metric: real-time colour-code decoding
before_after.after: under 1 µs per cycle up to distance 9

milestones.why_it_matters: Superconducting qubits are measured about a million times a second, so decoders must be fast and accurate. Real-time neural decoding removes the speed limit of the first AlphaQubit.

milestones.title: Equational Theories Project settles all 22 million magma law implications
milestones.summary: A Terence Tao-led online collaboration launched in September 2024 settled all 22,028,942 implications between the 4,694 simplest equational laws for magmas, combining human proofs with automated theorem provers such as Vampire and Prover9/Mace4, all checked in Lean. Large language models played only a minor role.

before_after.metric: Implications resolved among 4,694 laws

milestones.why_it_matters: A model for large-scale mathematics: many contributors plus automated provers, with a proof checker guaranteeing each of millions of results.

milestones.title: AI tools help pin down the exact answer to Erdős problem #1026
milestones.summary: An ambiguous 1971 Erdős question on monotone subsequence sums was made precise and answered online. Harmonic's Aristotle proved the square case in Lean on 7 December 2025, AlphaEvolve data suggested a formula for every length, and an AI literature search found a 2024 packing result that completed it. Terence Tao wrote up the full proof.
milestones.why_it_matters: A documented case of AI tools fitting into open collaborative mathematics, with formal proving, numerical exploration and literature search each checked by people.
milestones.contested_note: The square case Aristotle proved was already in Tidor, Wang and Yang (2016), whom erdosproblems.com credits with the first proof; Tao traces its packing idea to Seidenberg (1959). The final assembly relies on cited results and was not formalized.

sources.label: Terence Tao, The story of Erdős problem #1026 (2025-12-08)

milestones.title: GPT-5.2 Pro proves Gaussian maximum likelihood improves with more data
milestones.summary: Mark Sellke and Steven Yin report that GPT-5.2 Pro variants derived every result in their paper, the first nontrivial proofs that the maximum likelihood estimator's average log-loss never worsens with more data, for Gaussians with unknown covariance and Gamma variables with unknown scale. The Gaussian case was flagged open; humans only prompted and checked.
milestones.why_it_matters: Learning theorists had shown that extra data can hurt some learners; settling the textbook Gaussian case shows when the basic intuition holds, and the proofs came from the model.
milestones.contested_note: Not yet peer-reviewed; OpenAI says external experts reviewed the proofs.

sources.label: Sellke and Yin, On Learning-Curve Monotonicity for Maximum Likelihood Estimators, arXiv:2512.10220
OpenAI, Advancing science and math with GPT-5.2 (2025-12-11)

milestones.title: AI agent places first ahead of 804 humans in an AtCoder Heuristic Contest
milestones.summary: Sakana AI's ALE-Agent, a system making about 4,800 calls to GPT-5.2 and Gemini 3 Pro, entered the four-hour AtCoder Heuristic Contest 058 on 14 December 2025 by special permission, unrated, and took first place among 804 human entrants with an approach that beat the problem setter's intended solution. It cost about US$1,300.
milestones.why_it_matters: Heuristic contests reward open-ended optimisation, close to real engineering problems like scheduling and routing, rather than puzzles with known answers.

sources.label: AtCoder contest history for ALE-Agent's account (rank 1 in AHC058)

milestones.title: NOAA puts AI global forecast models and a hybrid AI-physics ensemble into use
milestones.summary: NOAA deployed three AI-based global systems built from a fine-tuned GraphCast: AIGFS, whose 16-day forecast uses 0.3% of the GFS's computing; a 31-member AI ensemble with early skill gains of 18-24 hours; and a 62-member hybrid AI-physics ensemble that beat both on most metrics. NOAA notes weaker hurricane intensity forecasts in version 1.

before_after.metric: Computing for a 16-day global forecast

milestones.why_it_matters: The US national weather service now runs AI forecasts operationally, and blending AI and physics ensembles points to a way of keeping the strengths of both.

milestones.title: MASAI trial: AI-supported mammography finds more cancers, misses no more
milestones.summary: Sweden's MASAI trial randomized 105,934 women to AI-supported screening (Transpara triaging scans to single or double reading) or standard double reading. AI found 29% more cancers (6.4 vs 5.0 per 1,000) with 44% less reading; interval cancers were non-inferior (1.55 vs 1.76 per 1,000) and sensitivity rose from 73.8% to 80.5%.

before_after.metric: Screening sensitivity

milestones.why_it_matters: Finding more cancers only helps if no more are missed between screens. A large randomized trial showing both, with far less radiologist time, is strong evidence for real screening programs.

sources.label: The Lancet (interval cancers, primary endpoint), 2026-01-31 issue

milestones.title: AI resolves Erdős problem #728 with a Lean proof, essentially autonomously
milestones.summary: Erdős problem #728 on factorial divisibility was vaguely stated; once a precise version was agreed, Kevin Barreto ran GPT-5.2 Pro and Harmonic's Aristotle, which produced a Lean proof by 6 January 2026. It was described as the first Erdős problem resolved essentially autonomously by AI; Pomerance's 2014 paper uses a similar method.
milestones.why_it_matters: Marked the shift from AI rediscovering known results to AI producing new, machine-checked solutions to problems collected from one of the most prolific mathematicians.

sources.label: Sothanaphan, writeup of Aristotle's proof, arXiv:2601.07421
Tao et al., AI contributions to Erdős problems (wiki)

milestones.title: LLM agent runs multistage experiments on Berkeley's Advanced Light Source
milestones.summary: Berkeley Lab's Accelerator Assistant, an agent driven by large language models, turns plain-language requests into executable plans: retrieving archived data, finding control channels, writing scripts, operating the accelerator within safety limits and analyzing results. On the Advanced Light Source it cut experiment preparation about 100-fold versus an expert's manual scripting.

before_after.metric: time to prepare an experiment workflow
before_after.after: a few minutes from one prompt (about 100× faster)

milestones.why_it_matters: Big facilities lose scarce beam time to setup work. Agents that safely turn intent into machine operations could let scientists run more, and more complex, experiments.
ai_systems: Accelerator Assistant (LLM agent built on the Osprey framework)

milestones.title: AISLE's AI analyzer credited with all 12 flaws in OpenSSL's Jan 2026 fixes
milestones.summary: OpenSSL's 27 January 2026 security advisory fixed 12 vulnerabilities, all reported by AISLE researchers (one also found independently by another researcher), who say their autonomous AI analyzer found them. One was high severity (a stack overflow in CMS message parsing), some date back to 1998, and AISLE's fixes were adopted for 5 of the 12.
milestones.why_it_matters: OpenSSL secures much of the internet's encrypted traffic and is heavily audited. An AI system finding every flaw in a release shows how far automated auditing has come.

milestones.title: AlphaGenome predicts regulatory effects of DNA variants from 1 million bases
milestones.summary: AlphaGenome reads 1 million bases of DNA and predicts thousands of functional genomic tracks at up to single-base resolution, including gene expression, chromatin accessibility, transcription-factor binding and splicing. Trained on human and mouse genomes, it matches or beats the strongest external models in 25 of 26 variant-effect evaluations.
milestones.why_it_matters: Most disease-linked DNA changes lie outside genes, in regulatory regions. One model scoring a variant across many layers of regulation helps researchers prioritize which changes matter.

sources.label: Google DeepMind blog, 2025-06-25 (preprint announcement; updated for Nature)

milestones.title: AxiomProver proves Fel's conjecture with a formal Lean proof
milestones.summary: Axiom Math's AxiomProver, given a natural-language statement, produced a complete Lean/Mathlib proof of Fel's conjecture, an explicit formula for syzygy invariants of numerical semigroups. Axiom says no hints, helper lemmas or manual patches were added after kickoff; humans wrote the statement, definitions and the accompanying paper.
milestones.why_it_matters: An open conjecture went from statement to machine-checked proof without human mathematical input, so correctness rests on the Lean checker rather than trust in the AI.

milestones.title: Sixteen Claude agents write a C compiler that builds the Linux kernel
milestones.summary: Nicholas Carlini ran 16 Claude Opus 4.6 agents in parallel, mostly unsupervised, over nearly 2,000 sessions and about $20,000 of API use. Without internet access they wrote a 100,000-line Rust C compiler that builds a bootable Linux 6.9 on x86, ARM and RISC-V and passes about 99% of most compiler test suites.
milestones.why_it_matters: A compiler is a large, tightly specified system. Agents building one from scratch show autonomous teams can deliver big, testable software; output slower than unoptimized GCC shows the limits.
milestones.contested_note: Anthropic lists limits: it calls GCC for 16-bit real-mode boot code, uses GCC's assembler and linker, and emits code slower than GCC with optimizations off. Chris Lattner (Modular, 2026-02-18) called it a competent textbook implementation tuned to pass tests rather than build general abstractions.

sources.label: Anthropic Engineering, Building a C compiler with a team of parallel Claudes (2026-02-05)
Chris Lattner, The Claude C Compiler: what it reveals about the future of software (2026-02-18)

milestones.title: Claude Opus 4.6 finds 500+ high-severity bugs in heavily fuzzed open-source code
milestones.summary: Anthropic's red team ran Claude Opus 4.6 in a virtual machine with standard tools against open-source projects and validated more than 500 high-severity vulnerabilities, some missed for decades despite years of fuzzing. Examples in Ghostscript, OpenSC and the CGIF library are now patched by maintainers; human researchers validated each finding and wrote the first patches.
milestones.why_it_matters: Fuzzers miss bugs that need reasoning about code history or an algorithm's logic; finding them at scale helps under-resourced maintainers fix flaws before attackers find them.
milestones.contested_note: The 500+ count is Anthropic's own. Most reports were still in disclosure and the work focused on memory-corruption bugs, so the total cannot yet be checked independently.

sources.label: Anthropic Frontier Red Team, Evaluating and mitigating the growing risk of LLM-discovered 0-days (2026-02-05)

milestones.title: Aletheia agent writes a research paper without human intervention
milestones.summary: Google DeepMind's Aletheia, built on an advanced Gemini Deep Think, generates, checks and revises proofs in natural language. It wrote a paper on 'eigenweights' in arithmetic geometry with no human intervention. Run on 700 'open' Erdős problems, 137 of 200 gradable answers were flawed; of 13 meaningful ones, 4 were new and 9 already known.
milestones.why_it_matters: Moves AI from competition problems into the real research workflow of finding literature, proving and writing, with explicit accounting of what was autonomous.

milestones.title: GPT-5.2 conjectures formula showing single-minus gluon amplitudes are nonzero
milestones.summary: A preprint by Guevara, Lupsasca, Skinner, Strominger and Weil shows tree-level gluon amplitudes with one negative-helicity gluon, usually presumed zero, are nonzero in special 'half-collinear' kinematics. Per the paper, GPT-5.2 Pro first conjectured the key all-n formula, a new internal OpenAI model proved it, and the authors checked it by hand.

before_after.metric: single-minus tree-level gluon amplitudes
before_after.after: nonzero closed-form formula in half-collinear kinematics

milestones.why_it_matters: Scattering amplitudes are the core predictions of particle theory. A language model supplied the key conjecture and proof, though the result covers a narrow, unphysical-signature regime.
ai_systems: Internal OpenAI model (a scaffolded GPT-5.2, per OpenAI)
milestones.contested_note: Not yet peer reviewed. D. Louapre (Hugging Face blog, 2026-02-19) calls the AI conjecture a real contribution but stresses the narrow scope (measure-zero kinematics in (2,2) signature), says the physics framing was human work, and says the AI workflow is under-documented.

milestones.title: Claude finds the construction for Knuth's Hamiltonian cycle problem
milestones.summary: Donald Knuth reported that Claude Opus 4.6, prompted and coached by Filip Stappers, found in about an hour a rule splitting the arcs of a digraph on m³ vertices into three Hamiltonian cycles for every odd m. Knuth wrote the proof, which Kim Morrison checked in Lean; GPT models later settled even m.

before_after.metric: Values of m with a known general decomposition
before_after.before: m = 3 proved; 4 ≤ m ≤ 16 found by computer search
before_after.after: All odd m (Claude's rule, proved); even m ≥ 8 soon after via GPT-5.3-codex and GPT-5.4 Pro

milestones.why_it_matters: One of computing's most respected figures, previously sceptical of generative AI, documented an AI solving a problem he had worked on for weeks.

milestones.title: AI agents write and formally verify a zlib-compatible compressor in Lean
milestones.summary: With loose human supervision, Claude-based coding agents wrote a zlib-format DEFLATE compressor and decompressor in the Lean language and proved, checked by Lean's kernel, that decompressing compressed data returns the original for every input and compression level (given a size limit). The proof spans over 1,100 theorems in about 32,000 lines.
milestones.why_it_matters: As AI writes more of the world's code, people need guarantees it is correct. Machine-checked proofs let anyone confirm the result without trusting the AI that produced it.

milestones.title: Viazovska's sphere-packing proofs in dimensions 8 and 24 formally verified
milestones.summary: Math Inc.'s Gauss joined a Lean project begun by Sidharth Hariharan and Maryna Viazovska, proving all remaining 8-dimensional results in five days (announced 23 February 2026), then formalized the 24-dimensional proof in about two weeks from the original paper alone. The roughly 200,000-line release also fixed a typo in the published paper.

before_after.metric: Lean formalization of optimal sphere packing

milestones.why_it_matters: First machine-checked verification of Fields Medal-winning work; the team had estimated six more months for dimension 8 alone with existing tools.

milestones.title: Evo 2 DNA model scores genetic variants without task-specific training
milestones.summary: Evo 2, from Arc Institute, NVIDIA and others, is a 40-billion-parameter DNA model trained on about 9 trillion bases with a 1-million-base context. It scores genetic variants, including BRCA1 variants, without task-specific training. Zero-shot human gene-essentiality prediction is modest (AUROC 0.66), within the range of simple conservation scores.
milestones.why_it_matters: A DNA model needing no per-task training could help read mutation effects in any species, though its own gene-essentiality result shows clear limits.

milestones.title: Claude Opus 4.6 finds 22 Firefox vulnerabilities in two weeks
milestones.summary: Working with Mozilla, Anthropic used Claude Opus 4.6 to scan nearly 6,000 Firefox C++ files. In two weeks it found bugs that led to 22 CVEs, 14 rated high severity, almost a fifth of the high-severity Firefox vulnerabilities fixed in 2025, plus 90 other bugs. Most fixes shipped in Firefox 148.
milestones.why_it_matters: Browsers are among the most attacked and most tested programs. Mozilla found the reports easy to reproduce, showing AI auditing adds value even to mature, heavily fuzzed code.

milestones.title: AlphaEvolve raises lower bounds for nine classical Ramsey numbers
milestones.summary: Google researchers used AlphaEvolve to evolve search programs that build graphs with no large cliques or independent sets. They raised lower bounds for nine Ramsey numbers, such as R(3,13) from 60 to 61 and R(4,19) from 213 to 219, five in March and four more by April, and recovered every known exact lower bound.

before_after.metric: Lower bound on Ramsey number R(4,19)

milestones.why_it_matters: Ramsey records usually come from bespoke searches and can stand for years. One AI meta-method finding many improvements points to a general tool for extremal constructions, each easy to check.

sources.label: Nagda, Raghavan, Thakurta, Reinforced Generation of Combinatorial Structures: Ramsey Numbers, arXiv:2603.09172

milestones.title: AI-assisted stroke decision support cuts repeat vascular events in 77 hospitals
milestones.summary: In a cluster-randomized trial across 77 Chinese hospitals (21,603 ischaemic stroke patients), a decision-support system combining AI imaging analysis, stroke-cause classification and guideline recommendations cut new vascular events at 3 months from 3.9% to 2.9% (HR 0.74), without more bleeding. Disability and mortality did not differ.

before_after.metric: New vascular event within 3 months

milestones.why_it_matters: Shows AI-based support can improve hard patient outcomes at scale in ordinary hospitals by helping clinicians apply proven treatments more consistently.
ai_systems: Stroke clinical decision support system with AI imaging analysis
organizations: Beijing Tiantan Hospital, Capital Medical University
China National Clinical Research Center for Neurological Diseases

milestones.title: Hurricane center's 2025 review ranks Google DeepMind's AI model among the best
milestones.summary: Google DeepMind's experimental cyclone ensemble, shown live to US National Hurricane Center forecasters from June 2025, was assessed in NHC's official 2025 verification. Its ensemble mean (GDMI) slightly beat NHC's own Atlantic track forecasts at 12-72 hours, was the best Atlantic intensity model, and beat NHC's eastern Pacific track forecasts at 48-120 hours.

before_after.metric: Atlantic track skill at 12-72 h, 2025 season
before_after.before: NHC official forecast best of all guidance
before_after.after: GDMI slightly better than NHC official

milestones.why_it_matters: Hurricane track and strength decide who evacuates. An independent government review finding an AI model at or above expert forecasts is strong evidence it helps protect lives.
ai_systems: Google DeepMind Weather Lab experimental cyclone model (ensemble mean GDMI)

sources.label: Google DeepMind blog, Weather Lab launch, 2025-06-12

milestones.title: 30,000 Claude agents formalize a 500-page graduate textbook in Lean in a week
milestones.summary: Researchers at Meta FAIR and École des Ponts ran about 30,000 Claude 4.5 Opus agents in parallel on a shared code base to formalize Darij Grinberg's 500-plus-page graduate algebraic combinatorics textbook in Lean: 130,000 lines and 5,900 declarations, with all 340 target definitions and theorems formalized, in one week for about $100,000.
milestones.why_it_matters: Formalizing new research needs foundational texts in Lean faster than volunteers can write them; converting a whole graduate textbook automatically shows that bottleneck can be lifted.

sources.label: Gloeckle et al., Automatic Textbook Formalization, arXiv:2604.03071

milestones.title: Anthropic reports Claude Mythos Preview found thousands of zero-day bugs
milestones.summary: Anthropic said Claude Mythos Preview found thousands of high- and critical-severity vulnerabilities across every major operating system and browser, including a 27-year-old OpenBSD bug and a 16-year-old FFmpeg flaw, and wrote working exploits. Reviewers matched its severity ratings exactly in 89% of 198 checked reports; under 1% were patched at announcement.

before_after.metric: Working Firefox JavaScript-engine exploits in Anthropic's test harness (sandbox removed)

milestones.why_it_matters: AI that finds and weaponizes flaws at this scale shifts the balance between attackers and defenders, so Anthropic restricted access to organizations patching critical software (Project Glasswing).
milestones.contested_note: AISLE (blog, 2026-04-07) reported that small open-weight models, given the isolated vulnerable code, detected the flagship FreeBSD bug and, in one case, the core OpenBSD bug chain, arguing the capability is less exclusive than claimed. Most findings were undisclosed and unpatched, so the totals cannot yet be checked independently.

milestones.title: Firefox 150 ships fixes for 271 bugs found with Claude Mythos Preview
milestones.summary: Mozilla's Firefox 150, released 21 April 2026, fixed 271 security bugs that its pipeline found with an early Claude Mythos Preview: 180 rated sec-high, 80 moderate and 11 low, including a 20-year-old XSLT memory bug and several sandbox escapes. Firefox 148 had fixed 22 security bugs found with Claude Opus 4.6.

before_after.metric: Security bugs found with Claude and fixed in one Firefox release

milestones.why_it_matters: A heavily fuzzed, mature browser shipped hundreds of AI-found security fixes in one release, showing defenders can now use these models to harden critical code at scale.
milestones.contested_note: Severity ratings rest on crash symptoms, not confirmed exploits. Advisory MFSA 2026-30 groups internally found bugs into rollup CVEs, so the 271 do not appear individually; Mozilla's 7 May post reconciles the counts.

sources.label: Mozilla Hacks, Behind the Scenes Hardening Firefox with Claude Mythos Preview (2026-05-07)

milestones.title: GPT-5.4 Pro output yields new method resolving Erdős primitive-set problems
milestones.summary: An autonomous GPT-5.4 Pro run produced the first proof of Erdős problem #1196 in April 2026. Alexeev, Barreto, Lichtman, Price, Tao and coauthors turned its idea, Markov chains with von Mangoldt weights, into a method proving #1196 and #1217, a short proof of the Erdős Primitive Set Conjecture and a revised Banks–Martin conjecture.
milestones.why_it_matters: An AI-suggested idea, overlooked since Erdős's 1935 paper, became a reusable method settling several problems at once: AI contributing technique, not just answers.

milestones.title: AlphaEvolve cuts Spanner write amplification 20% and software size nearly 9%
milestones.summary: A year after launch, Google DeepMind reported that AlphaEvolve refined the compaction heuristics of Spanner, Google's global database, cutting write amplification by 20%, and found compiler strategies that shrank software's storage footprint by nearly 9%. It is now a regular tool in TPU design and found cache policies in two days rather than months.

before_after.metric: Spanner write amplification

milestones.why_it_matters: Writing less data per request means longer-lasting drives and lower costs in one of the world's largest databases. AI-found optimizations are becoming routine production engineering.

milestones.title: OpenAI model disproves Erdős's 1946 unit distance conjecture
milestones.summary: An internal OpenAI model constructed, in one shot, planar point sets with at least n^(1+δ) unit-distance pairs (fixed δ>0, infinitely many n), refuting Erdős's 1946 conjecture of n^(1+o(1)). The proof uses infinite class field towers. Nine mathematicians including Alon, Gowers and Tsimerman published a checked, simplified version; humans soon improved the exponent.

before_after.metric: Max unit distances among n planar points (lower bound)
before_after.before: n^(1+c/log log n), believed optimal since 1946

milestones.why_it_matters: Gowers wrote he would have recommended it to the Annals of Mathematics without hesitation; it overturned an 80-year-old belief in discrete geometry using number theory few expected to apply.

sources.label: OpenAI, Planar point sets with many unit distances (2026-05-20)
Alon, Bloom, Gowers et al., Remarks on the disproof

milestones.title: Formal proof-search agents resolve 9 open Erdős problems in Lean
milestones.summary: Google DeepMind evaluated LLM agents that write Lean proofs on open problems at scale. The strongest autonomously resolved 9 of 353 open Erdős problems with Lean statements, at a few hundred dollars each, and proved 44 of 492 OEIS conjectures; a simpler generate-and-check agent matched the Erdős results but cost more on the hardest problems.
