milestones.why_it_matters: Every claimed solution is machine-checked, so AI results can be trusted at scale and low cost, turning plausible text into guaranteed proofs.

milestones.title: GPT-5.5 Pro helps improve the high-dimensional lattice packing bound
milestones.summary: Abuya, Gargava and Zhao proved lattice sphere packings of density at least c·N²·log log N·2^(−N) in infinitely many dimensions N, beating Klartag's bound by a log log N factor. Prompted by Zhao, GPT-5.5 Pro proposed the approach and proved the bound; the other two authors had pursued a similar idea, and all three verified it.

before_after.metric: Lattice packing density lower bound

milestones.why_it_matters: Dense high-dimensional packings underpin coding theory and lattice cryptography; an AI combined two leading techniques into a result experts then checked.

milestones.title: Deep learning reads plant regulatory DNA in Arabidopsis and transfers to maize
milestones.summary: One neural network trained on 568 Arabidopsis DNA-binding datasets covering 46 transcription-factor families predicts where regulators bind DNA. Of 7,364 trait-linked variants, 20.72% were predicted to gain or lose binding sites; reporter assays on 340 constructs supported several predictions. The model also transferred to maize heat-stress data.
milestones.why_it_matters: Many crop-trait variants sit in regulatory DNA, not genes. Predicting how they alter transcription-factor binding could help pinpoint causal variants, even in species with little data.
organizations: Max Planck Institute for Plant Breeding Research

milestones.title: Neural networks design proteins that bind two drugs, with 100% and 83% success
milestones.summary: Dana-Farber and Harvard researchers paired two neural networks in a design loop to make proteins from scratch that bind two chemically distinct drugs, exatecan and apixaban, with success rates of 100% and 83%. The tightest had picomolar-to-nanomolar affinity, and the exatecan binder protected the drug's labile lactone ring from hydrolysis for days.

before_after.metric: Affinity of tightest binder versus next-leading method

milestones.why_it_matters: Proteins that grab small molecules can deliver drugs, sense them or catalyze reactions. Zero-shot design with high success cuts the trial and error that limited earlier methods.

milestones.title: OpenAI model proves the 50-year-old cycle double cover conjecture
milestones.summary: OpenAI released a three-page proof, credited entirely to GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra, that every bridgeless graph has a family of cycles covering each edge exactly twice, a 1970s conjecture of Tutte, Itai and Rodeh, Szekeres and Seymour. Sang-il Oum and Jim Geelen wrote expositions, Johannes Carmesin confirmed it, and Lean formalizations exist.
milestones.why_it_matters: One of graph theory's best-known open problems fell to a short argument built on classical flow theorems, suggesting some famous conjectures are hard to spot rather than deep.
milestones.contested_note: Correctness is not disputed. Thomas Bloom noted that using nowhere-zero F₂³-flows on cubic graphs to study cycle double covers goes back at least to Bermond, Jackson and Jaeger (1983).

sources.label: OpenAI, A proof of the cycle double cover conjecture (PDF, 2026-07-10)
Johannes Carmesin, The cycle double cover theorem, The Matroid Union (2026-07-21)

milestones.title: AI-found, Lean-checked sharp lemma for Erdős Problem 875 (partial)
milestones.summary: An OpenAI model (gpt-5.6-sol) in Doug Colkitt's harness proved four lemmas about the best known construction for Erdős Problem 875; Claude Fable 5 critiqued them. The key one, Lean-checked, doubles the safe 'carry' radius from about m/4 to exactly ⌈m/2⌉ and shows one step further fails. The problem itself remains open.

before_after.metric: Proven carry radius for block C_m = {1+i(m+1)} modulo m²+m+1
before_after.before: |u| < m/4, plus quotient window |w| < m/2 (GPT-5.5 Pro and Mazur, May 2026)

milestones.why_it_matters: It shows a two-model pipeline (one AI proves, a rival AI attacks) producing small, formally checked results, and maps exactly how far the current method for this Erdős problem can go.
ai_systems: Anthropic Claude Fable 5 (adversarial critique, Lean formalisation session)
milestones.contested_note: Lean covers Propositions 1–2 only (authors' claim; not rebuilt here); Propositions 3–4 are paper proofs. No human review; not posted on the erdosproblems.com thread as of 2026-10-14.

sources.label: GPT-5.5 Pro and L. Mazur, erdos_875 (prior result)

milestones.title: Claude Fable 5 finds a counterexample to the 1939 Jacobian conjecture
milestones.summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge posted a degree-7 polynomial map in three variables, credited to Claude Fable 5, whose Jacobian determinant is the constant −2 yet which is generically three-to-one, so it has no inverse. This disproves the Jacobian conjecture in every dimension above two; the two-variable case remains open.
milestones.why_it_matters: An 87-year-old conjecture, the target of many failed proofs, was settled by a machine-found example that anyone can check with computer algebra in seconds.
milestones.contested_note: The counterexample is not disputed, but how it was found has not been disclosed. Adrian Vasiu said an AI-written exposition borrowed notation and ideas from an unpublished Borisov–Gabber–Vasiu draft; Alpöge later said their method deserves credit too (Wikipedia).

sources.label: Terence Tao, A digestion of the Jacobian conjecture counterexample (2026-07-21)
The Conversation, 'hello there the jacobian conjecture is false thanx' (2026-07-22)

milestones.title: Claude Mythos Preview finds new attacks on HAWK signatures and 7-round AES
milestones.summary: Anthropic reported two attacks found largely by Claude Mythos Preview. A lattice symmetry cuts expected key recovery for HAWK-256, challenge parameters of a NIST post-quantum signature candidate, from 2^64 to 2^38 operations. A new meet-in-the-middle attack on 7-round AES-128 runs 200–800 times faster than the best before. Full AES is unaffected.

before_after.metric: Expected key-recovery cost for HAWK-256

milestones.why_it_matters: Encryption standards rest on years of expert attack. An AI weakening a post-quantum candidate in about 60 hours of work shows such review can be greatly accelerated before deployment.
milestones.contested_note: Daniel Apon said the reduction checks out (NIST pqc-forum, 28 July), but no independent end-to-end key recovery is reported. HAWK-512 and HAWK-1024 stay exponential (about 2^108 and 2^182). The HAWK work had occasional human guidance, and Anthropic's validators were not cryptography specialists.

sources.label: Anthropic, Discovering cryptographic weaknesses with Claude (2026-07-28)
Implicator.ai, Anthropic posts AI-found HAWK attack to NIST forum (2026-07-29)

milestones.title: OpenAI internal model claims ten advances with Lean-checked proofs
milestones.summary: OpenAI released a 249-page manuscript and Lean 4 formalizations of ten results by an unreleased internal model (reported as Astra), including an explicit non-sofic group, a counterexample to Connes's rigidity conjecture, Ehrhart's volume conjecture, better sphere-packing upper bounds, and Erdős problems 146, 180 and 183. None is peer-reviewed.
milestones.why_it_matters: If they hold, these settle decades-old questions across algebra, geometry and complexity; Lean certificates let anyone check the logic, though statement fidelity still needs human review.

milestones.title: Claude proves over two thirds of zeta zeros are simple and on the critical line
milestones.summary: Asked by a non-mathematician to attack the Riemann hypothesis, an unreleased Claude model running about 60 subagents proved that over two thirds (67.25%) of zeta's nontrivial zeros are simple and on the critical line, up from 5/12. Two Anthropic mathematicians checked it, a Lean proof followed, and Youness Lamzouri found a simpler one.

before_after.metric: Proven share of zeta zeros that are simple and on the critical line

milestones.why_it_matters: The share of zeros proven on the critical line is a standard yardstick of progress toward the Riemann hypothesis; this moves it past two thirds, though it does not lead to a proof.
milestones.contested_note: Not yet peer-reviewed. The argument builds on unconditional pair-correlation results of Aryan and of Baluyot, Goldston, Suriajaya and Turnage-Butterbaugh; Lamzouri calls Claude's version intricate, with a mechanism that is not immediately transparent.

sources.label: Anthropic, Claude improves a lower bound on zeta zeros on the critical line (2026-08-10)
Alpöge and Furman, More than two thirds of the zeta zeros are simple and on the critical line, arXiv:2608.13637
Lamzouri, A new proof that more than 2/3 of the zeros are simple and on the critical line, arXiv:2609.02882

milestones.title: AlphaEvolve helps lower the matrix multiplication exponent to ω < 2.371177
milestones.summary: Google DeepMind researchers, with Josh Alman and Virginia Vassilevska Williams, reformulated the optimization problem inside the laser method's 'combination loss analysis', solved it with a new gradient-based optimizer and refined that solver with AlphaEvolve. The result lowers the best upper bound on the matrix multiplication exponent ω from 2.371339 to 2.371177.

before_after.metric: Upper bound on the matrix multiplication exponent ω

milestones.why_it_matters: ω sets the asymptotic cost of multiplying matrices and of the many algorithms that reduce to it; each small improvement has taken years of human work.
milestones.contested_note: About 0.97×10⁻⁴ of the 1.6×10⁻⁴ gain came from the reformulation and gradient-based optimizer before AlphaEvolve was applied.

sources.label: Dupont et al., Improving the matrix multiplication exponent with modern optimization and AlphaEvolve, arXiv:2608.16884

milestones.title: AxiomProver formalizes in Lean that prime gaps of at most 246 recur forever
milestones.summary: Axiom Math released a Lean 4 proof, produced by its AxiomProver system from a human-written blueprint and curated by its team, that infinitely many consecutive primes differ by at most 246. It covers Maynard's sieve and the Polymath8b refinement that cut the bound from 600 to 246, assuming only the Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem.
milestones.why_it_matters: 246 is the best proven step toward the twin prime conjecture; a reusable machine-checked library of sieve methods lets later work on prime gaps build on verified foundations.
milestones.contested_note: This formalizes known results rather than proving new ones; the Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem is assumed rather than formalized, and people wrote the blueprint.

sources.label: Axiom Math, Lean formalization of bounded gaps between primes
IEEE Spectrum, AI used to verify toughest mathematics proof yet (2026-08-17)

milestones.title: Claude-written Lean proof: no percolation at the critical point in any dimension
milestones.summary: On 28 August 2026 Anthropic's Justin Leder posted to Anthropic's GitHub a Lean proof, written autonomously by Claude models under his direction, that critical bond percolation on Z^d has no infinite cluster for any d ≥ 2, by proving a 2024 gluing conjecture of Gady Kozma and Shahaf Nitzan. Dimensions 3 to 10 were open.

before_after.metric: Dimensions where θ(p_c) = 0 is proven

milestones.why_it_matters: Whether three-dimensional percolation has a continuous phase transition was a central open problem of probability theory; one expert said solving it would earn a Fields Medal.
milestones.contested_note: Not refereed. Kozma awaits a human-readable version; Ahmed Bou-Rabee calls it clever but without substantial new ideas (Quanta, 1 Oct). Arthur Blanc-Renaudie posted a short human proof built from the AI's ideas. The files are no longer on the repository's main branch, and Anthropic has made no announcement.

sources.label: Blanc-Renaudie, Notes on Kozma and Nitzan's proof of θ(p_c)=0, arXiv:2610.10502
Scientific American, AI solves a 'holy grail' problem from probability theory (2026-09-30)

milestones.title: State model predicts how cells respond to perturbations in unseen contexts
milestones.summary: Arc Institute's State predicts how genetic, signalling and chemical perturbations change gene expression across cell contexts. Its cell embeddings are trained on observational data from 167 million cells. The authors report more than 30% better discrimination of perturbation effects than baselines on large datasets, and introduce the Cell-Eval evaluation framework.
milestones.why_it_matters: A reliable virtual cell would let researchers test perturbations on screen before costly experiments, but independent benchmarks so far show the problem is hard.
milestones.contested_note: Ahlmann-Eltze et al. (Nature Methods, 2025-08-04) tested earlier deep-learning perturbation models, not State, and found none beat simple linear baselines. State's authors say it is the first to consistently beat such baselines (Arc Institute, 2025-06-23); we found no independent head-to-head test.

milestones.title: Complete male fly nervous system mapped: 166,700 neurons in brain and nerve cord
milestones.summary: HHMI Janelia, Google Research, Cambridge and collaborators published the connectome of a whole male fruit-fly central nervous system, brain plus nerve cord: 166,700 fully proofread neurons in 11,710 types, about 125 million synaptic connections (Google figure). AI helped trace neurons and humans proofread. Sex differences concentrate in higher brain centres.
milestones.why_it_matters: A complete brain-and-cord map lets scientists follow sensory input to motor output end to end and compare the sexes at synaptic resolution.

milestones.title: Claude agents produce first complete Lean proof of Fermat's Last Theorem
milestones.summary: Dozens of Claude agents, working largely autonomously for 11 days, wrote about 13 million lines of Lean proving Fermat's Last Theorem along the Frey–Serre–Ribet–Wiles–Taylor route, with 29,500 theorems in the final proof. It rests only on Lean's three standard axioms; Kevin Buzzard reviewed it. It formalizes Wiles's proof rather than finding a new one.

before_after.metric: Machine-checked proof of FLT

milestones.why_it_matters: One of mathematics' deepest proofs is now checked line by line by computer, suggesting AI can make verifying frontier mathematics routine.

milestones.title: AI-assisted, Lean-checked proofs show forced 3D Euler flows can blow up
milestones.summary: Tristan Buckmaster (NYU) and Levent Alpöge (Anthropic) posted proofs that the 3D incompressible Euler equations, the 2D Boussinesq system and the porous-medium equation can form finite-time singularities under a smooth external force, extending Córdoba and Martínez-Zoroa's method. Claude and OpenAI's Codex helped heavily; Claude wrote all the Lean, which uses only standard axioms.
milestones.why_it_matters: Blow-up for the frictionless Euler equations is a recognized stepping stone toward the Navier–Stokes Millennium problem, and here the whole argument is machine-checked.
milestones.contested_note: Not peer-reviewed. Terence Tao called it a remarkable achievement with significant AI input, released earlier than planned because of external events. The force is an added ingredient; the unforced problem stays open.

sources.label: Science News, AI may have solved one of math's biggest puzzles (2026-09-09)

milestones.title: Neural-network search finds a candidate stable blow-up for unforced 3D Euler
milestones.summary: Anima Anandkumar's Caltech group used a physics-informed neural network, steered away from trivial solutions and refined with splines for certified error bounds, to find an approximate self-similar blow-up of the 3D Euler equations in free space, with no boundary or force. It appears numerically stable; a rigorous stability proof is still missing.
milestones.why_it_matters: Unforced blow-up in free space is the version fluid experts care most about; a precise, stable candidate is the usual first step toward a computer-assisted proof.
milestones.contested_note: Terence Tao (Mathstodon, 2026-09-08): a promising candidate that appears numerically stable, but a rigorous demonstration of stability is still lacking and may need enormous effort.

sources.label: Anima Anandkumar, Stable singularity of the Euler equations on R^3 without forcing (2026-09-07)

milestones.title: OpenAI claims Lean-checked forced blow-up for Navier–Stokes, a Clay problem
milestones.summary: OpenAI said an internal model, running about 10,000 agents at a time, produced a 166-page proof that 3D Navier–Stokes flow starting from rest can reach unbounded velocity in finite time under a smooth, compactly supported force, an option the Clay problem allows. It released a Lean formalization and will not claim the $1 million prize.
milestones.why_it_matters: If it stands, it settles a Millennium Prize problem as stated, but only through a forced version experts call unnatural; the unforced question that matters most for fluids stays open.
milestones.contested_note: Experts in Scientific American (21 Sept) call the forcing a loophole; Constantin, Ignatova and Vicol (arXiv:2609.20803) show such constructions need a non-analytic force at the singularity. Bastounis, Circelli and Hansen (arXiv:2610.08144) argue the Lean code does not match the written proof. Buckmaster disputes credit; OpenAI denies using his work.

milestones.title: Claude-found algorithm refutes the 3SUM and APSP hypotheses
milestones.summary: Asked to check cryptographic constructions, an internal Claude model instead discovered, in a 16-million-token session with no human input, an algorithm refuting the 3SUM, APSP and Exact Triangle hypotheses. Josh Alman and Virginia Vassilevska Williams simplified and extended it: deterministic 3SUM in O(n^1.9992) and APSP in O(n^2.9995) time. Anthropic Lean-checked the main theorems.

before_after.metric: Time exponent for 3SUM on polynomial-size integers

milestones.why_it_matters: Many conditional lower bounds in fine-grained complexity assumed 3SUM and APSP need essentially quadratic and cubic time. Refuting both reshapes the field and speeds up many reducible problems at once.
milestones.contested_note: Lean covers Theorems 19 and 22 and the zero-weight case of Corollary 39; real-input and some other results are not formalized. Not yet peer-reviewed.

milestones.title: Humans and AI agents sharpen the AI-claimed integer multiplication exponent
milestones.summary: OpenAI's manuscript (dated 23 September, released 6 October 2026) claimed n-bit integer multiplication in O(n(log n)^(1−κ)) time on a multitape Turing machine with κ = 2^−182. In an open repository maintained by Douglas Colkitt, contributors and their AI agents raised κ to about 0.00167 (≈2^−9.2), still conditional on that unreviewed framework.

before_after.metric: Exponent saving κ in O(n(log n)^(1−κ))

milestones.why_it_matters: If the framework holds, it beats the n log n bound conjectured optimal since 1971, and shows people and AI agents openly compounding a machine-generated idea within days.

milestones.title: Machine-written proof that ω ≤ 9/4 passes independent Lean checks
milestones.summary: OpenAI's 6 October release included an internal-model proof, dated 2 October, that n×n complex matrices can be multiplied with O(n^(9/4+ε)) arithmetic operations, far below August's 2.371177. The Big O Speedrun tracker rebuilt OpenAI's Lean proof from source and kernel-checked it against its exact problem statement.

milestones.why_it_matters: It would be far larger than any improvement since 1990. A kernel-checked proof makes the claim hard to dismiss, though experts have yet to review the mathematics.
milestones.contested_note: No published expert review as of 2026-10-14; Scientific American (8 Oct) reported no independent check of the mathematics. The result is asymptotic and gives no faster practical algorithm.

milestones.title: OpenAI releases 722 machine-written mathematics manuscripts
milestones.summary: OpenAI posted 722 manuscripts in 372 result families from an unreleased internal model, using about three hours of compute per result across roughly 4,000 posed problems. Claims include the Unique Games Conjecture, Hodge for CM abelian varieties and integer multiplication below n log n. None is peer-reviewed; about 42% of top-line results have Lean proofs.
milestones.why_it_matters: Research-level mathematics at industrial scale shifts the bottleneck from finding proofs to checking them; the corpus is a public test of how much machine mathematics survives.
milestones.contested_note: On 2026-10-07 OpenAI withdrew three manuscripts after a sign error broke a Weil-class argument, and revised 14 others (openai/math history.md). The repository itself warns unformalized results could have issues; ASKA's 2026-10-07 review found most of the corpus unverified.

milestones.title: OpenAI model's Lean proof: zeta has no zeros with real part above 7/8
milestones.summary: A manuscript in OpenAI's 6 October release, dated 30 September, claims every Dirichlet L-function, the Riemann zeta function included, has no zeros with real part above 7/8, the 'quasi-Riemann hypothesis'. Its Lean proof of the zeta and Dirichlet statements was independently rebuilt with no errors. Contributors' agents have since posted claimed refinements to 0.874861.

before_after.metric: Zero-free half-plane Re s > θ for the Riemann zeta function
before_after.before: none known (only regions shrinking toward Re s = 1)

milestones.why_it_matters: No zero-free half-plane for zeta of any width was known; one gives a power-saving error term when counting primes. It is not the Riemann hypothesis, which needs 1/2.
milestones.contested_note: Not peer-reviewed. OpenAI says its zeta work did not follow its standard procedure and a companion write-up was human-edited. The Hecke L-function part is not in Lean, and the refinements are unchecked. Hector Pasten told Scientific American some see it as progress toward Riemann, others not.

milestones.summary: An open search stacking all available TESS sectors for 4.04 million FGKM dwarfs, plus nearby K/M dwarfs and TOI hosts, finds transits too weak to see in any one sector. Its 13 October 2026 update lists 671 counted candidates, up from 533 earlier that day, including a possible third planet around TOI-4342. None is confirmed.

milestones.why_it_matters: It shows a small independent team, working with an AI coding agent, can mine public mission data at full scale and release reproducible candidates for others to check.

milestones.title: Codex-assisted note lifts the one-sample matroid prophet guarantee to 2⁻³¹
milestones.summary: OpenAI's manuscript showed that, with one past sample per item and an all-seeing adversary choosing the order, a fixed rule always earns some constant fraction of the best possible team, about 2⁻²⁹³. Working with Codex, Ryan Shea's written proof raises it above (35/32)·2⁻³¹. The proof has exact checks but no review or formalization.

before_after.metric: Guaranteed fraction of the expected offline optimum (one-sample, almighty adversary)

milestones.why_it_matters: It shows AI assistants tightening the loose constants that machine-written proofs often leave behind. The guarantee is still tiny and the proof is unreviewed.
milestones.contested_note: Only same-agent checks so far. The repo also notes an unverified public claim of 2⁻⁴⁷ by another author on 8 Oct.

milestones.why_it_matters: Computer-checked certificates turn 'is there a smaller example?' into a finite search anyone can rerun, although only within one construction template.

milestones.title: Agent-driven entrants push Lean-verified 3SUM to n^1.962 and APSP to n^2.99556
milestones.summary: Within a week of the 3SUM and APSP preprint, people pointing AI agents at it submitted better exponents to the Big O Speedrun verifier, which rebuilds each Lean proof and checks it against a fixed statement. milestones.why_it_matters: Kernel-checked leaderboards let anyone with AI agents contribute to frontier algorithms and be trusted without peer review, compressing incremental progress into days.

milestones.title: AI-assisted search finds a 106-gate AES S-box circuit (AND/XOR/XNOR model)
milestones.summary: A companion AI-assisted preprint gives an AES S-box circuit of 106 gates (depth 24) against 110 on NIST's list, an inverse S-box of 109 gates against 112, and 121 gates at depth 16 against 125. All are exhaustively checked and Lean-proved; comparisons hold only for AND/XOR/XNOR gates, not richer gate sets.

before_after.metric: AES S-box gate count, {AND, XOR, XNOR} model

milestones.why_it_matters: The S-box is the main nonlinear cost of AES, the world's most widely used cipher. Smaller circuits mean cheaper encryption hardware and faster bitsliced software.

milestones.title: AI-assisted search shrinks the AES-field multiplier from 117 to 112 gates
milestones.summary: A preprint by Swapnil Jain, using AI-assisted computational search, gives an AND/XOR circuit for multiplication in the AES field GF(2^8) with 112 gates at depth 6, versus 117 in the 2010 Circuit Minimization Team record, plus 107 gates at depth 13. Each AES-field circuit is exhaustively checked and Lean 4 kernel-proved.

before_after.metric: Gates for GF(2^8) AES-polynomial multiplication at depth 6

milestones.why_it_matters: Field multipliers are building blocks of encryption and error-correcting codes. Fewer gates make bitsliced and masked cryptography cheaper, and machine-checked proofs mean nobody has to trust the search.

milestones.title: Claimed proof: the GF(2) Möbius transform needs fewer XORs than Yates' 1937 recipe
milestones.summary: Swapnil Jain's repository claims, with written proofs, certificates and partial Lean, that the subset-parity (Möbius) transform over GF(2) can use asymptotically fewer XOR gates than Yates' ½·N·log₂N butterfly, by moving an AI-generated Fourier-transform construction into bit arithmetic. The saving only appears for astronomically large inputs.

before_after.metric: XOR gates for the GF(2) Möbius transform on N = 2^k inputs

milestones.why_it_matters: It answers, if it holds, a question Boyar and Find asked in 2013: whether letting terms cancel can beat the classic recipe. The answer would be yes, but only at sizes no computer will reach.
milestones.contested_note: Not disputed, but only AI referees have read it; no human referee yet. The main theorem is not in Lean (92 supporting theorems are).

milestones.title: Lean-checked proof lifts the exact Fourier transform speed-up to δ = 0.00123
milestones.summary: OpenAI's 25 September preprint computed the exact discrete Fourier transform in O(n(log n)^(1−δ)) steps with δ = 10⁻¹³. Within a week, people working with AI assistants raised δ repeatedly. Ryan Shea fitted Jeremy Kothe's community circuit into the formal framework, reaching δ = 0.0012331685, which the public leaderboard rebuilt and kernel-checked in Lean.

before_after.metric: Exponent saving δ in O(n(log n)^(1−δ)) for the exact DFT (Lean-verified)

milestones.why_it_matters: A machine-written result was improved about 12 billion-fold in a week by people and AI tools, and every step was checkable by computer. The gain is theoretical: no faster FFT software follows.

milestones.title: Exact fold carries a loose ball-and-rod crystal into the densest packing
milestones.subfield: discrete geometry; rigidity theory; sphere packing
milestones.summary: A framework of balls joined by rigid rods, arranged like the boron net of calcium hexaboride, folds continuously into the densest stacking of equal balls. No rod stretches and no balls overlap, while density rises steadily from 0.2233 to 0.7405 (pi/sqrt18). An explicit formula and an exact certificate of 16,240 nonnegative coefficients cover every instant.

milestones.contested_note: Not disputed. Reviewed only internally by AI models, with no human referee. The framework family is prior art (Borcea and Streinu 2021, section 7), and historical priority of the motion is unresolved. It is a geometry result, not a predicted phase change in real CaB6.
